items.prompt: Mrs. Hu is an English teacher at a high school. Christmas is coming, and she is planning a game, “Secret Santa,” in her class. Here is a note about the game.Note:1. Ask every student to fill out a card with their names and hobbies.2. Put all the cards in a box. Then, every student has to take out a card from the box and find their “lucky person.” Remind students not to tell anyone the names on their cards. Also, make sure nobody gets their own card.3. The game will last for a week. Secret Santa needs to give gifts to his or her “lucky person.”4. Every Secret Santa must leave a clue with every gift.5. At the end of the week, all the students have to find out their Secret Santa with those clues. remind 提醒 clue 線索（ ）1. What does “Secret Santa” have to do? (A) Teach students at school. (B) Give some gifts to a classmate. (C) Help the teacher with lesson plans. (D) Buy gifts for every classmate.（ ）2. What should the students write down on the cards at first? (A) Some notes and key points of the lesson. (B) The colors of their cards. (C) Their names and hobbies. (D) The names and hobbies of their Secret Santa.
choices: Give some gifts to a classmate.
Help the teacher with lesson plans.
Buy gifts for every classmate.（ ）2. What should the students write down on the cards at first?
Some notes and key points of the lesson.
The names and hobbies of their Secret Santa.
items.explanation: 1. 由 Note 第三點，Secret Santa 要做的任務是須送禮物給他們一起玩遊戲的同學。2. 由 Note 第一點可知，學生們一開始要在卡片上寫的是他們的名字和嗜好。

items.prompt: KK School NewsBadminton Star Meet-and-Greet 2024-10-20 Do you play badminton? Do you love it? If so, you know Sarah from Class 803 for sure. She is a skillful badminton player. And in fact, she is the NO. 1 badminton player of the junior high school students in Taiwan now. We are proud to know her and have her on the school team.Get ready to meet Sarah：•10 / 26 (Sat.) 10 a.m. ~ 11:30 a.m.•Student Activity CenterListen to Sarah share her stories. You can shake hands and take photos with her.Come and join us! Meet-and-Greet 見面會 activity center 活動中心（ ）1. Look at the pictures. Who is NOT “skillful”? (A) (B) (C) (D) （ ）2. What might Sarah say? (A) Students, it’s time for the PE class. Let’s play badminton today. (B) I don’t like sports at school very much. In fact, I’m not good at sports. (C) Oh, come on. Give me a break. I can’t play badminton, and I don’t like it. (D) I must thank my dad for this. He teaches me, helps me, and practices with me.（ ）3. What can we learn from the reading? (A) The meet-and-greet will start at about 11 o’clock in the morning. (B) Sarah is on the school badminton team, and she is a good player. (C) The students in KK School are not proud of Sarah. No one likes her. (D) Sarah is a senior high school student, and she helps the school team of KK School.
choices: Students, it’s time for the PE class. Let’s play badminton today.
I don’t like sports at school very much. In fact, I’m not good at sports.
Oh, come on. Give me a break. I can’t play badminton, and I don’t like it.
I must thank my dad for this. He teaches me, helps me, and practices with me.（ ）3. What can we learn from the reading?
The meet-and-greet will start at about 11 o’clock in the morning.
Sarah is on the school badminton team, and she is a good player.
The students in KK School are not proud of Sarah. No one likes her.
Sarah is a senior high school student, and she helps the school team of KK School.
items.explanation: 1. 由後句可知 Sarah 是目前全臺灣國中生排名第一的羽毛球選手，可推知是一位很優秀、出色的選手，並且對羽毛球是很熟練的。從圖片各個人物的表現，僅有廚師不符合。2. 由 Listen to Sarah share her stories. 可知 Sarah 會在這次見面會分享她的故事，因此內容會與她的個人歷程以及幫助過她的人有關，其他選項皆不符合現況的描述。3. 由 We are proud to know her and have her on the school team. 可知，Sarah 有參加校隊。

items.prompt: Dear parents and students,Welcome to KS Junior High School! In the school year of 2025, we are very excited to have all of you with us.KSJH is a new school in the city. There are nine classes in each grade. There are about 500 students and 60 teachers in the KSJH big family. So, don’t worry! You are in good hands. On top of that, we are famous for our basketball team, the Eagle. It is a strong team. We are happy that there are some great players joining us this year.Here is a map of the school. There is a mountain and a pond behind the school. Students of KSJH can learn about nature right at school. This is very special in the city. It’s also why we are one of the best schools in the city.To know more about KSJH, we are inviting all of you to a school tour next Saturday. After the tour, there will be a party, and I will be happy to answer all the questions then. There will be food and drinks at the party, too. Please reply to this mail, and let us know how many people we will expect from your family. Thank you!Sincerely,Jaqueline MurphyKSJH Principal tour 導覽 reply 回覆 principal 校長（ ）1. What is between the gym and the swimming pool? (A) The classrooms. (B) The playground. (C) The basketball court. (D) The mountain and the pond.（ ）2. There are about ＿＿＿ students in one class in KSJH. (A) forty (B) twenty-nine (C) eighteen (D) twelve（ ）3. Who might get this mail? (A) Kevin. He is a new student of KSJH. (B) Judy. She is a big fan of Team Eagle. (C) Ms. White. She is a teacher at KSJH. (D) Mr. Johnson. He is a parent of a 6-year-old child.
choices: The mountain and the pond.（ ）2. There are about ＿＿＿ students in one class in KSJH.
twelve（ ）3. Who might get this mail?
Kevin. He is a new student of KSJH.
Judy. She is a big fan of Team Eagle.
Ms. White. She is a teacher at KSJH.
Mr. Johnson. He is a parent of a 6-year-old child.
items.explanation: 1. 由地圖可知，「籃球場」在體育館及游泳池之間。2. 由第二段第二到三句可知，KS 國中每個年級有九個班，且全校共有約 500 名學生，推算後每班學生人數約為 18-19 人。3. 閱讀全文可知，此信是寄給即將就讀 KS 國中的新生及其家長。

items.prompt: My brother is a cook. I didn’t know what a cook was like until I visited him at his restaurant today. First, cooks go to the market early in the morning to get the freshest ingredients. After a short break, there is a meeting about the day’s menu. Everyone can decide the special of the day. Today, it is expensive seafood from the market. Then, when everything is ready, the restaurant is open. It will be the busiest time of the day. There are many people at the restaurant today. Waiters and waitresses are welcoming the guests. In the kitchen, I help my brother take the seafood out of the refrigerator. The other cook is mixing the soup. There are two helpers doing the dishes. And my brother even lets me cut tomatoes. It’s really fun! I think my brother is a great cook. I want to be a cook when I grow up, too. ingredient 食材 seafood 海鮮（ ）1. Which is true about the writer’s brother? (A) He is a farmer. Olivia：＿3.＿ I won’t do that myself.------------------------------------------------------(Ten minutes later)Tom：Does that happen very often?Amy：Yes. Many groups release animals here. Tom：That will lead to ＿4.＿.Amy：True. These groups’ actions are terrible for the Earth.Amy：Look! There’s a dying fish. ＿5.＿, give me a hand, ＿5.＿. Let’s save it and set it free.Tom：No problem. release 釋放（ ）1. (A) Let’s (B) Let (C) Do not (D) Let’s not（ ）2. (A) How are they doing? (B) That’s the rule here. (C) It’s kind of you to do so. (D) Welcome back. We miss you.（ ）3. (A) The animals are happy. (B) Let’s not catch fish here. (C) Watch out for the animals. (D) I’m sorry for that.（ ）4. (A) different rules (B) many kinds of animals (C) a lot of problems (D) some dos and don’ts（ ）5. (A) Tom; please (B) Please; Tom (C) Don’t; please (D) Don’t; Tom

items.explanation: 1. 由 Not again. 可知，此句應是「不要」放生動物在湖裡，否定祈使句的句型為「Do not / Don’t＋原形動詞...」。2. 由 Amy 說「不要把動物放生進湖裡」及「看到那個標誌嗎？」可知，此處 Amy 最可能會說「那是這裡的規則」。3. 由後句「我自己將不會做那種事」可知，此處 Olivia 應是說「我覺得很遺憾」。4. 由 Amy 後句回應「那些團體的行為對地球有害」可知，此句 Tom 應是說那些團體的放生行為將導致「許多問題」。5. 由第一個空格後及第二個空格前皆有逗號可知，第一個空格是「人名」，第二個空格是 please。

Uncle Fred is rich now! We used to sleep in his small old home.Cindy：Yeah. Hey, what are those?Greg：They are sheep. Look, Uncle Fred is very happy in the picture. Oh, I miss him.Cindy：Where is he now? Can’t you tell?Greg：Hmm... In the picture, I see a kangaroo with those sheep.Cindy：Australia! Let’s go see Uncle Fred and his big beautiful home in Australia.Greg：No, Cindy. Read here. In the newspaper, people in that big house thanked Uncle Fred. He is a farmer there. newspaper 報紙 No way! 不可能！ rich 富有的 used to 過去曾經 miss 想念 Can’t you tell? 你看不出來嗎？ kangaroo 袋鼠 Australia 澳洲 house 房子（ ）1. What do we know about Greg and Cindy? know 知道 (A) They are happy to see Uncle Fred in his old home. (B) They are reading a book. (C) They miss Uncle Fred. (D) They are in Australia.（ ）2. Which is NOT in the picture? which 哪一個 (A) Some sheep. (B) Greg and Cindy. (C) Uncle Fred. (D) A kangaroo.（ ）3. Which is true about the home in the picture? (A) It’s in Australia. (B) It’s small and old. (C) It’s Greg and Cindy’s. (D) It’s Uncle Fred’s home.

They are in Australia.（ ）2. Which is NOT in the picture? which 哪一個

items.explanation: 1. 兩人看到的是 Uncle Fred 在報紙上的照片，並非親自見到 Uncle Fred；對話一開始 Greg 叫 Cindy 查看報紙上的照片，可知兩人在看報紙；由 Greg 說 I miss him 及後文 Cindy 表示要到澳洲看 Uncle Fred 可知，兩人並不在澳洲，但可推知兩人想念他。2. 由於對話中談論照片內容時，除了 Uncle Fred 外，另提及 his big new home、sheep、a kangaroo，可知照片中並沒有 Greg 和 Cindy。3. 因 Cindy 和 Greg 根據照片內容猜測 Uncle Fred 人在澳洲，可知照片裡，又大又新的房子也應在澳洲；且對話中僅提到 Uncle Fred 是農夫，而對話最後表示 people in that big house thanked Uncle Fred，可推知此房子不屬於 Uncle Fred，因此選項 (C)、(D) 皆不正確。

People are waiting for today’s show. It’s at ＿4.＿. Wake up, everyone. ＿5.＿ prepare for the show. We are going to put on a great show tonight! circus 馬戲團 strong 強壯的 favorite 最喜愛的 food 食物 show 表演（ ）1. items.prompt: (On the phone)Willy：What’s wrong, Hank?Hank：Oh, I can’t sleep at night. Some ＿1.＿ are in my house!Willy：Hey, clean your house! It’s scary!Hank：My house is OK!Willy：Then ＿2.＿Hank：They are Mr. Brown’s pets! His house is next to my home.Willy：You can talk to Mr. Brown. He is nice.Hank：Well… His rabbits come to my house, too. And his birds are now in my trees…Willy：No way! Hank：Yes, ＿3.＿. Oh, no! Not again! ＿4.＿ are those? what’s wrong 怎麼了 can’t 不能 house 房子 clean 清理 scary 可怕的 then 那麼 next to 在……旁邊 talk to… 和……講話 No way! 不可能！（ ）1. (A) mouse (B) mice (C) sheep (D) horses（ ）2. (A) who are they? (B) what are in your house? (C) are those Mr. Brown’s pets? (D) where are those small animals from?（ ）3. (A) that’s true (B) they are cute (C) these toys are cute (D) no wonder Mr. Brown is sad（ ）4. (A) How (B) How old (C) Who (D) What
choices: where are those small animals from?（ ）3.
no wonder Mr. Brown is sad（ ）4.
items.explanation: 1. 由空格後的 be 動詞 are，可知空格應填入複數名詞；而後句提到 scary 及 clean your house，可推知是家裡有「老鼠」。2. 根據後文說明是隔壁鄰居 Mr. Brown 的寵物，可知此題是接續前面「家中有老鼠」的問題，詢問「那些小動物從哪裡來的？」。3. 由 Hank 先表示 Yes.，可推知後句應為肯定語氣，故用 that’s true。4. 由 Hank 喊出 Oh, no! Not again! 可推知，他又看見有動物造訪他家，並疑惑這次又是「什麼」動物，疑問詞用 what。

Ted is a doctor. He is busy, but he never misses a class. Sam and Amy are young students. They are brother and sister. Mei is from Taiwan. She is a Chinese teacher. Isn’t that cool? Everyone is different, but they all like to dance. practice 練習 learn 學習（ ）1. It’s 10 o’clock on Monday morning, who is in Jennifer’s classroom? (A) Ted. (B) Mei. (C) Mrs. Wu. (D) Sam and Amy.（ ）2. items.prompt: Best Pet in the World Real dogs are cute, but they can be noisy. They run all the time. We have a special pet for you. Check out the new robot dog, K-9. Its size is the same as a real dog, and its design is great for you.At Home: A Good Friend. K-9 is smart. It can listen to you. It can play songs and take photos for you. Can it play? Yes, it can. It can play games with you. It is clean and quiet.On the Road: A Smart Friend. K-9 can walk with you on the sidewalk. It can watch out for traffic lights. Is the light red? K-9 can wait. What about oncoming cars? Don’t worry. K-9 can see them. It can’t talk, but it can make sounds to warn the user. You are safe with K-9.Take K-9 home today! best 最好的 as 如同 clean 乾淨的 worry 擔心 sound 聲音 safe 安全的（ ）1. What is this reading about? (A) A smart robot dog. (B) A cute song about dogs. (C) A new smartphone design. (D) A special dog from the USA.（ ）2. What CAN’T K-9 do on the road? (A) Run all the time. (B) Walk on the sidewalk. (C) Check the traffic lights. (D) Warn the user about cars.（ ）3. Which is NOT true about K-9? which 何者 (A) It is smart, clean, and safe. (B) It can play songs and take photos. (C) It is not a real dog, but they are the same size. (D) It is for traffic only, and it can’t play with users.
choices: A special dog from the USA.（ ）2. What CAN’T K-9 do on the road?
Warn the user about cars.（ ）3. Which is NOT true about K-9? which 何者
It is smart, clean, and safe.
It can play songs and take photos.
It is not a real dog, but they are the same size.
It is for traffic only, and it can’t play with users.
items.explanation: 1. 由第一段第四句「看看這隻新的機器狗 K-9」可知，應選 (A)。2. 由第一段可知，真狗「總是跑來跑去」，而第三段指出 K-9 則是 walk（走）和 wait（等待），它是安全的嚮導，不會像真狗一樣亂跑，故選 (A)。3. 文章分為 At Home 和 On the Road 兩部分，At Home 的部分指出「它可以跟你玩遊戲」。因此 (D) 說它「只適用於交通」且「不能跟使用者玩」有誤。

items.unit: L6_Are There Any Shelves Outside the Door？
items.prompt: 填入適當字詞：1. A：Are ＿＿＿＿＿＿ any blue pens next to the book? B：No, there are ＿＿＿＿＿＿.2. ＿＿＿＿＿＿ not a blanket in the dining room, but there ＿＿＿＿＿＿ two in the bedroom. 3. A：Is there ＿＿＿＿＿＿ apple on the table?B：＿＿＿＿＿＿, there is.
items.answer: 1. there; not 2. There’s; are 3. an / one; Yes
items.explanation: 1. 由答句 there are 可知，問句也要用 there 問，故第一格填入 there；由 No 可知，為否定簡答，故第二格填入 not。2. 由 not 及 there 可知，是在講「飯廳裡沒有毛毯，但臥室裡有兩條」，故第一格填入 There is 的縮寫 There’s，而第二格填入複數 be 動詞 are。3. 由單數名詞 apple 可知要搭配數量詞 one 或不定冠詞 an 表示「一顆」；由 there is 可知為肯定簡答，故第二格要填入 Yes。

items.prompt: 填入正確的字詞：1. A：＿＿＿＿＿＿ is this? B：＿＿＿＿＿＿ a monkey. 2. A：What ＿＿＿＿＿＿ these? B：＿＿＿＿＿＿ sheep.3. A：＿＿＿＿＿＿ that? B：＿＿＿＿＿＿ apple.
items.answer: 1. What; It’s 2. are; They’re 3. What’s; An
items.explanation: 1. 由 a monkey 可知是問「什麼」，故第一格要用 What；第二次提到 this 常用 it 代替，故第二格要用 It is 的縮寫 It’s。2. 由 these 可知主詞為複數，故第一格要用複數 be 動詞 are；由問句可知 sheep 在此為複數，由於 these / those 與 are 不能縮寫，故第二格用 They’re。3. 由 apple 可知是問「什麼」，故第一格要用 What is 的縮寫 What’s；apple 為單數且為母音開頭，故第二格要用 An。

items.prompt: The fox and the elephant live in a forest. They are good friends. One day, the King of the forest, the lion, says, “Let’s have a running competition in the forest. The fastest animal can marry my beautiful daughter.” The fox and the elephant are very happy. They like the lion’s daughter a lot. On the day of the running competition, the fox calls the elephant. “Sorry, brother. I am so sick. I can’t go to the competition,” the fox says. “Are you OK? Is there anyone at your house now?” the elephant asks. “No. My parents are not home. But that’s OK. I can take care of myself,” says the fox. “The poor fox. He is my friend. I should take care of him,” the elephant thinks. So, the elephant goes to the fox’s house with some fresh fruit and hot soup instead. But, on his way to the fox’s house, he hears the news about the fox. That is, the fox won the competition and he can marry the lion’s daughter. The elephant is sad. He and the fox are not friends anymore. live 住 forest 森林 say 說 fastest 最快的 marry 娶 call 打電話 sick 病的 can’t 無法 ask 詢問 take care of 照顧 think 想 instead 相反地 hear 聽到 won 贏 anymore 不再（ ）1. Who is the winner of the running competition? winner 贏家 (A) The fox. (B) The lion. (C) The elephant. (D) The lion’s daughter.（ ）2. What is a “competition”? (A) A lion. (B) A book. (C) A game. (D) A tree.（ ）3. Which is true? which 哪一個 (A) The fox isn’t sick. (B) The fox can’t run fast. (C) The elephant is at the lion’s home. (D) The elephant can marry the lion’s daughter.
choices: The lion’s daughter.（ ）2. What is a “competition”?
A tree.（ ）3. Which is true? which 哪一個
The elephant is at the lion’s home.

items.explanation: 1. 由倒數第三句可知，賽跑的贏家是狐狸。2. 由後句「最快的動物可以娶獅子的女兒」可知，competition 指「競賽」，故選 game 最適合。3. 由文中可知，狐狸有去參加賽跑，可推知他沒有生病。

items.prompt: Last Saturday, the weather was warm and sunny. The students of Class 803 went to Blue Mountain Park for a class trip. At ten o’clock, everyone was having a great time in the forest. Peter and his friends were climbing a tall tree because they wanted to see a bird’s nest. Near the river, Lily and her classmates were sitting on the grass. They were sharing their snacks and talking about their favorite songs. Their teacher, Mr. Wang, was preparing a map for their next walk. Suddenly, there was a strange noise in the bushes. A small, thin monkey ran out. It looked very weak and hungry. Peter wanted to give it some bread, but Mr. Wang stopped him. He pointed to a sign on a tree. It said, “Do not feed the monkeys. It is not allowed here. Let them find their own food.” Mr. Wang told the students to stay back and be quiet. At that moment, the small monkey was crying for help. A few minutes later, a large monkey jumped down from a tree. It was the mother! She took her baby and went back into the forest. Everyone felt happy. Although they didn’t feed the monkey, they learned a good lesson about nature. trip 旅行 nest 巢 grass 草地 suddenly 突然 strange 奇怪的 bush 灌木叢 weak 虛弱的 bread 麵包 feed 餵 allow 允許 tell / told 告訴 moment 時刻 although 雖然 lesson 教訓（ ）1. items.explanation: 1. 由全文描述可知，學生在森林公園觀察猴子並學習到不餵食野生動物的自然課題，故選 (A)。2. 由第一段第五跟第六句可知，Lily 跟她的同學正在聊天吃零食，故選 (B)。3. 雖然文中未明確描述原因，但根據情境推論，在野生動物（小猴子）出現且需要母猴帶回時，保持安靜是為了不驚擾動物。4. (A) 由第二段第三句可知，Peter 並未餵食小猴子；(B) 由第二段倒數第三到第五句可知，母猴是回來找他的小孩，故正確；(C) 由第一段最後一句可知，Mr. Wang 是為了步行而準備地圖，不是迷路；(D) 由第一段第一句可知，當天是晴天。

I’m meeting a friend there later.Ben：Sure, it’s just around here. Walk down Maple Street to Main Road. It’s on your left and right on the corner. You can’t miss it.Julie：Cool! By the way, when I came out of the metro station, I saw a coffee shop. Is it good?Ben：I’m not sure, but there is a restaurant on Oak Street. Where is the restaurant?Ben：It’s across from a bank and next to a hotel.Julie：How do I get there from here?Ben：You can go along this way, turn left at the coffee shop, and keep walking to Main Road. items.prompt: When is a good time for you to visit Japan? Many people might choose spring because of the cherry blossoms. People from around the world come to visit, and Japanese people also enjoy sitting under the cherry blossom trees. People in different areas of Japan may see the flowers at different times because the weather plays an important role. Down south, it gets warmer early, so the flowers start blooming in late March. Sometimes people can even see them in early March because the weather in spring of that year is warmer than it is in that season of other years. On the other hand, if you want to see snow early, you will have to go north. Kushiro starts getting cool in October, and in December, it’s usually only 3°C. However, something happened. When the race __2.__, he took off. Soon, I was right behind him. Then there was a pain in my leg, so I stopped running. When my brother saw that, __3.__. He put his arm around me, and we finished the race together. I was so touched when my brother helped me walk to the finish line. “Thanks, Rick,” I said to my brother. take / took off 起跑 soon 很快 pain 疼痛 touched 受感動的 finish line 終點線（ ）1. items.prompt: We often see plastic in our lives. We use plastic bottles, bags, and boxes every day. When plastic stays in nature for a long time, it breaks into very small pieces. These pieces are microplastics. They are very small, and people cannot see them easily. Microplastics are in rivers, seas, fish, and even drinking water. When fish eat microplastics, the plastic stays inside them. Then, when we eat the fish, the plastic goes into our bodies. In early 2025, a study in Nature Medicine brought some bad news. The research team found about 7 grams of microplastics in some people’s brains. This is about the same weight as five bottle caps or one plastic spoon. There is much more plastic in the brain than in other parts of the body. The study also showed one more thing: people with memory problems had even more microplastics in their brains. Because of this, doctors and scientists ask people to use less plastic. By changing daily habits, people can help protect their health and the environment. when 當……時 microplastic 塑膠微粒 easily 輕易地 research 研究 brain 大腦 cap 瓶蓋 spoon 湯匙 than 比…… part 部分 memory 記憶 scientist 科學家 less 更少的 daily 日常的 environment 環境（ ）1. What is the main idea of this reading? main 主要的 (A) People can easily see microplastics and clean them up. (B) Scientists found a way to take microplastics out of the human brain. (C) Microplastics are getting into human brains and may bring health problems. (D) Microplastics only stay in rivers and fish, not in human bodies.（ ）2. Which is true? (A) There are no microplastics in our drinking water. (B) The research team found 7 grams of microplastics in fish. (C) Doctors ask people to eat less fish to protect their health. (D) People with memory problems have more microplastics in their brains.（ ）3. What does “weight” mean? mean 意指 (A) How long something is. (B) How fast something moves. (C) How heavy something is. (D) How old something is.
choices: People can easily see microplastics and clean them up.
Scientists found a way to take microplastics out of the human brain.
Microplastics are getting into human brains and may bring health problems.
Microplastics only stay in rivers and fish, not in human bodies.（ ）2. Which is true?
There are no microplastics in our drinking water.
The research team found 7 grams of microplastics in fish.
Doctors ask people to eat less fish to protect their health.
People with memory problems have more microplastics in their brains.（ ）3. What does “weight” mean? mean 意指
items.explanation: 1. 第一、二段介紹塑膠微粒的來源及如何進入人體，第三段點出醫學期刊的研究結果，第四段總結並呼籲減塑。綜觀全文，故選 (C)。2. 由第三段最後一句「people with memory problems had even more microplastics in their brains（有記憶問題的人大腦中有更多的塑膠微粒）」，故選 (D)。3. 由瓶蓋和湯匙的比喻，可推論出 weight 指的是物品的「重量」，故選 (C)。

The following shows the plans. mobile phone operator 電信公司 unlimited 不受限制的 limited 定量的 fee 費用 contract 合約 Internet speed 網速 data 流量 within the network 網內 outside the network 網外 local call 市內電話（ ）1. Tony wants unlimited speed and some free minutes for local calls. Which plan should he choose? (A) Plan A. (B) Plan B. (C) Plan C. (D) Not any one of the three.（ ）2. Tony’s father uses Plan C. He called outside the network for one minute and made a five-minute local call last month. How much does he have to pay? (A) NT$299. (B) NT$499. (C) NT$529. (D) NT$599.（ ）3. Tony’s grandmother seldom uses her cellphone. She only uses it to send messages to her family. Which plan should she choose? (A) Plan A. (B) Plan B. (C) Plan C. (D) All of the plans.（ ）4. items.prompt: Sometimes, small pieces of ice fall from the sky during a heavy rain. These pieces are not snow; they are hail. Hail can be as small as a bean, or as large as a baseball. When hail falls, it can be very dangerous because it falls very fast. How does hail start? It usually happens during a thunderstorm. When warm air moves up into the cold sky, it carries water drops with it. In the very cold clouds, the water drops freeze into ice. The ice pieces move up and down in the clouds, and they get more layers of ice. When the ice pieces become too heavy for the wind to hold, they fall to the ground. Hail can lead to many problems. It can break car windows, damage the roofs of houses, and hurt farmers’ plants. In early 2024, a big hail storm in China damaged many fruit trees, and farmers lost a lot of money. Because hail is strong and heavy, it can also hurt people and animals if they stay outside. If you see hail, you must find a safe place immediately. Do not stay under a tree because branches may fall on you. The best way to stay safe is to run inside a strong building and stay away from windows. hail 冰雹 bean 豆子 dangerous 危險的 thunderstorm 雷雨 carry 攜帶 freeze 結冰 layer 層 window 窗 damage 損害 roof 屋頂 plant 植物 if 如果 branch 樹枝（ ）1. What is the best title for this reading? title 標題 (A) The History of Big Hail Storms in China (B) How to Collect Hail to Make Cold Water (C) Hail: The Dangerous Ice from the Sky (D) Why Hail Always Falls on Farmers’ Houses（ ）2. According to the reading, which is true? (A) Hail is a kind of snow. It falls during sunny days. (B) Every piece of hail is the same size as a small bean. (C) Staying under a tall tree is the best way to hide from hail. (D) Hail gets more layers of ice when it moves up and down in the clouds.（ ）3. What does the word “immediately” mean? (A) In the end. (B) Right away. (C) Under the weather. (D) Back and forth.
choices: The History of Big Hail Storms in China
How to Collect Hail to Make Cold Water
Hail: The Dangerous Ice from the Sky
Why Hail Always Falls on Farmers’ Houses（ ）2. According to the reading, which is true?

Every piece of hail is the same size as a small bean.

items.explanation: 1. 這篇文章全面地介紹了「冰雹」的定義、成因、造成的損害以及防護措施。2. (A) 第一段說「這些不是雪」，且冰雹通常發生在「雷雨」時，而非晴天；(B) 第一段提到冰雹大小不等，從小如豆子到大如棒球都有；(C) 最後一段警告不要待在樹下，因為樹枝可能會掉落。3. 前一段提到冰雹很危險，而此句前後提到「如果你看到冰雹」及「找到安全的地方」，可推知 immediately 應為「立刻」。

One of them was his or her partner. Then, 153 people and a computer decided how similar the six faces were to this person. The study showed that couples did not become more alike over time. Instead, they already looked similar at the beginning. This means people often choose someone with a similar face to be their partner. items.prompt: Melanie：Hey, you’re back! You were very sick last week.Tricia：Well, I couldn’t help that.Melanie：I know. You looked terrible last Monday.Tricia：I __1.__ terrible, too. __2.__, and I had a high fever then. To tell you the truth, I almost fainted.Melanie：What did the doctor say?Tricia：Not much. I __3.__, so he just gave me some medicine and told me to get some rest.Melanie：Getting rest is good. __4.__ I’m happy for you.Tricia：Thanks, I feel that way, too. back 回來 tell / told 告訴 truth 實話 almost 幾乎 faint 暈倒（ ）1. (A) feel (B) felt (C) feels (D) am feeling（ ）2. (A) I didn’t have a fever (B) My throat wasn’t sore (C) My knees didn’t hurt (D) I had a really bad headache（ ）3. (A) put on a coat (B) sent a message (C) took a bath (D) caught a cold（ ）4. (A) Now, I am sick. (B) You’re healthy again. (C) Right, I need more rest. (D) Medicine is not good for your health.

Medicine is not good for your health.
items.explanation: 1. 由前面 Melanie 說的話可知時間為上週一，動詞時態要用過去式。2. 由後句提到自己也發高燒，可推知前面應該也是描述另一個生病的症狀，故選「我頭真地很痛」。3. 醫生給了 Tricia 一些藥並要她多休息，可推知她是「感冒」。4. 前面提到 Tricia 已經回到崗位上，可推知 Melanie 會說「你又再次恢復健康了」才符合語意。

items.prompt: Fiona：What’s wrong with your voice? You sound like a man.Lela：I ＿1.＿ to concerts with my friends last Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, so I ＿1.＿ a sore throat now.Fiona：I see. ＿2.＿Lela：What happened? Are you OK now?Fiona：I went camping in the mountains in Hsinchu last Saturday. It was very cold ＿3.＿ the next day. Though I ＿4.＿ some medicine yesterday, my head still ＿4.＿ now.Lela：＿5.＿ Maybe you should put on a heavy coat next time you go camping in the mountains.Fiona：You’re right. sound like 聽起來像 concert 演唱會 though 雖然 （ ）1. (A) went; have (B) go; have (C) go; had (D) am going; am having（ ）2. (A) I didn’t go there last night. (B) But my throat wasn’t sore at all. (C) I had a sore throat last weekend, too. (D) I also went to a concert with my classmates last week.（ ）3. (A) , so I caught a cold (B) because I slept all day (C) , but I didn’t see a doctor (D) , and I really love camping（ ）4. (A) take; hurt (B) ate; hurt (C) took; hurts (D) eat; hurts（ ）5. (A) That’s too bad. (B) That’s really amazing. (C) It can last for two hours. (D) Why did you catch a cold?
choices: I didn’t go there last night.
But my throat wasn’t sore at all.
I had a sore throat last weekend, too.
I also went to a concert with my classmates last week.（ ）3.
, but I didn’t see a doctor
It can last for two hours.
Why did you catch a cold?
items.explanation: 1. 第一格由 last Friday, Saturday, and Sunday 可知，此處在談論過去的事，所以動詞須用過去式；第二格由 now 可知，動詞須用現在式。2. 由下句「發生了什麼事？你現在還好嗎？」可知，上句為「我上週末也喉嚨痛。」才符合語意。3. 由上下句意可知，「天氣冷」下句為「所以我隔天就感冒了。」才符合語意。4. 由 yesterday 可知，第一格動詞須用過去式，且 medicine 應搭配的動詞為 take；由 now 及 my head 可知，第二格的動詞須用第三人稱現在式。5. 由上下文意可知，「那太糟了。」才符合句意。

items.unit: L1_It Rained a Lot Yesterday
items.prompt: Today, we are here to say good-bye to our friend, Glacier Okjokull. Okjokull was in Iceland. In 1890, it ＿1.＿ 16 km2 but only 1 km2 in 2012. And now, it’s not there anymore. ＿2.＿ Yes, it helped keep our home cool. It was nice and cool here ＿3.＿. Now, it is always hot. ＿4.＿, we had the hottest summer again last year. We lose a lot of ice every year. When we have no glaciers anymore, the sea level will go up. This will take away our houses and put our lives in danger. We lost Glacier Okjokull. It is the first one, but it won’t be the ＿5.＿ one. We have to do more to stop climate change. glacier 冰河 anymore 再也不 hottest 最熱的 will 將會（ ）1. (A) is (B) was (C) does (D) were（ ）2. (A) Is the weather nice? (B) It is cold in winter. (C) It was a fishing town. (D) Was it our good friend? （ ）3. (A) still (B) around (C) before (D) too（ ）4. (A) Take a look (B) For example (C) From now on (D) At first（ ）5. (A) last (B) snowy (C) more (D) little
items.explanation: 1. 由前文過去的時間判斷此處應選過去式，又主詞為單數 it，過去式be動詞用 was。2. 由答句 Yes 及過去式判斷前句應為過去式問句，故選 (D)，其餘選項不合文意。3. 前句說明冰河讓該地維持涼爽，下句比較現在總是很熱，可知本句是描述「過去」的氣候，故選 (C)。4. 下文「舉例」說明去年是最熱的夏天，故選 (B)。5. but 連接前後語意相反的句子，前句表這是第一條消失的冰河，後句應為卻不是「最後」一條。

items.prompt: Good morning, Mr. and Mrs. Maxwell. My name is Jason Jones. Let me tell you about our hotel trips. Our popular one is a one-day trip to Rainbow Canyon. First, you will enjoy the view of Rainbow Canyon when you ride a raft down the river. Then you will have a delicious lunch at a barbecue restaurant. After that, you will visit an old village and experience the life there. Finally, our guide will take you to a special place. It’s a great place for watching beautiful animals in Rainbow Canyon. If that is too much, you might like our half-day trip to Topaz Lake. On this trip, you can go out on the water on your own boat. Also, you will get a free lunch, and you can eat that on the boat or back in the restaurant. After that, you will visit the same old village as the one-day trip. For each of our trips, our guide will drive you, show you around, and bring you back when you finish the trip. If you would like to join either of these tomorrow, please let me know by six o’clock tonight.＊Rainbow Canyon 彩虹峽谷 Topaz Lake 托帕斯湖 view 景色 ride a raft 乘木筏 barbecue 烤肉 village 村莊 experience 體驗 guide 導遊 if 如果 drive 開車（載） either（兩者中）任何一個（ ）1. Where might Jason Jones work? (A) In a zoo. (B) On a boat. (C) In a hotel. (D) In a restaurant.（ ）2. What is the same about the two trips? (A) They both last one day. (B) People can eat on the boat. (C) People have to drive by themselves. themselves 他們自己 (D) They both lead people to an old village.（ ）3. How will the Maxwells get to the places on the trips? (A) (B) (C) (D)
choices: In a restaurant.（ ）2. What is the same about the two trips?
People can eat on the boat.
People have to drive by themselves. themselves 他們自己
They both lead people to an old village.（ ）3. How will the Maxwells get to the places on the trips?
items.explanation: 1. 由第三句話「讓我說明本飯店的旅遊行程」，可推知 Jason Jones 是飯店員工。2. 由倒數第三句可知，兩個行程相同的地方是拜訪老村莊。3. 由倒數第二句可知，兩個行程皆由導遊開車接送。

It is near the train station with a nice view of Sunny Lake and the mountains. It is a good place to have fun. There is a fish pond behind the restaurant. My children enjoyed watching and feeding the fish there.Very Nice Meal(Lucy)It is a family-run restaurant. It is famous for its yummy fish and tea cakes. The food is great. What will Andrew most likely tell his friends about Lakeview Restaurant? most likely 最有可能地 (A) Don’t go there by car. (B) Its cakes are not so good. (C) Fish is not my favorite food. items.prompt: Jay fainted in the PE class in the morning one day. We thought he fainted because he was too tired. Why did we think so? Because Jay always played computer games all night after school. This time, the nurse told Jay, “You need to start a healthy diet right away and do some exercise every day, or you might be taken to the hospital next time.” Now, Jay seldom plays computer games and does exercise four times a week. (D) Jay went to the health center because he needed some rest.（ ）2. What does Jay do after his second visit to the health center? (A) He rests at home all day. (B) He often goes to the health center. (C) He changes his diet. (D) He studies every day to become a doctor.
choices: Jay fainted because he was too tired.

(C) Victor will leave for Japan soon. soon 很快地 (D) The trip will be too expensive for them.

items.prompt: Every year, my family takes a trip to a different country. This year, we decided to visit the USA. We got to New York City yesterday, January 23rd. After we checked in at the hotel, we went to Times Square. There are many theaters in and around Times Square, and we saw a musical, The Lion King, there. Then we rode bicycles to the Brooklyn Bridge. On the way there, we enjoyed many beautiful sights. I will always remember them. Tomorrow, we are going to have a museum day. In the morning, we will visit the Met. There are many wonderful works of art there, and I really want to see Monet’s and Picasso’s paintings. In the afternoon, we will go to the American Museum of Natural History. It was the setting for the successful movie, Night at the Museum. Maybe my legs will feel sore after I walk around these places all day, but I will learn a lot for sure.＊Times Square 時代廣場 Brooklyn Bridge 布魯克林大橋 Met大都會藝術博物館 American Museum of Natural History 美國自然史博物館 musical 音樂劇 ride 騎（車） bicycle 腳踏車 sight 景點 painting 畫作 history 歷史 setting 場景 successful 成功的（ ）1. What did the writer do on the first day in New York City? (A) They went to a park. (B) They watched a movie. (C) They visited a museum. (D) They left for Times Square.（ ）2. What will the writer do tomorrow? (A) They will see some paintings. (B) They will go to the Brooklyn Bridge. (C) They will watch Night at the Museum. (D) They will go shopping in a department store.（ ）3. What can we learn from this reading? (A) The writer didn’t visit New York City last year. (B) The writer could learn a lot about cooking on this trip. (C) The writer’s family didn’t go to New York City with him. (D) People can see Monet’s paintings in the American Museum of Natural History.
choices: They left for Times Square.（ ）2. What will the writer do tomorrow?
They will go to the Brooklyn Bridge.
They will watch Night at the Museum.
They will go shopping in a department store.（ ）3. What can we learn from this reading?
The writer didn’t visit New York City last year.
The writer could learn a lot about cooking on this trip.
The writer’s family didn’t go to New York City with him.
People can see Monet’s paintings in the American Museum of Natural History.
items.explanation: 1. 由第一段第四句可知，作者到飯店辦理入住後先去了 Times Square。2. 由第二段第一句可知，會去參觀博物館欣賞畫作。3. (A) 由「每年都會去不同的旅遊景點」可知，作者去年沒有造訪紐約；(B) 由兩天的行程看來，與烹飪相關性不大；(C) 由第一段前兩句可知，作者與家人同行旅遊；(D) 在大都會藝術博物館才會看到莫內的畫作，故選 (A)。

items.prompt: Kate：Amy, do you have to cook every day?Amy：No. I don’t like cooking. It’s too hot to stay in the kitchen.Kate：So, you often eat out, right?Amy：Not really. I live with my parents-in-law. They love cooking, and they are great at it, so I eat at home with them.Kate：You are so lucky! My husband doesn’t like eating out, so I have to cook every day.Amy：Why don’t you teach him to cook? That way, you two can take turns cooking.Kate：That’s a great idea. Why didn’t I think of that before? too... to... 太……以致於無法…… parents-in-law 公婆 lucky 幸運的 take turns 輪流（ ）1. Why DOESN’T Amy like cooking? (A) She enjoys eating out. (B) She is bad at cooking. Which is true? (A) Kate’s husband enjoys eating out. (B) Amy’s parents-in-law are good at cooking. (C) Kate doesn’t cook every day. (D) Amy doesn’t live with her parents-in-law.

items.prompt: Last winter, all the students in my class were sick. It all started with Bruce. He had a headache, a fever, and a sore throat, __1.__. Instead, he __2.__ to school, and six other classmates __2.__ the cold because they sat next to him. They didn’t stay home the next day, either, so more classmates got sick. On the third day, I had a headache and a sore throat. However, __3.__ I didn’t have a fever __3.__ I didn’t go to the hospital. I went to school as usual. By Friday, everyone had a cold. __4.__ Because people in our country don’t always see a doctor for a cold, we only do that for serious health problems. instead 取而代之 as usual 照常（ ）1. (A) because he was cold (B) and it was cold outside (C) so he didn’t see a doctor (D) but he didn’t rest at home（ ）2. (A) came; caught (B) comes; catches (C) is coming; catching (D) come; catch（ ）3. (A) because; , so (B) so,; because (C) so,; ╳ (D) ╳; , so （ ）4. (A) Why did I see a doctor? (B) Why didn’t we see a doctor? (C) How did all my classmates feel? (D) What happened to all my classmates after that?
choices: so he didn’t see a doctor
but he didn’t rest at home（ ）2.
Why did I see a doctor?
Why didn’t we see a doctor?
How did all my classmates feel?
What happened to all my classmates after that?
items.explanation: 1. 由下一句「相反地，他到學校來，且其他六個同學從他那裡染上感冒。」可推知，Bruce 雖然頭痛、發燒和喉嚨痛，「但他卻沒有待在家休息」才符合語意。2. 由上下文可知，此句依然在描述去年冬天的狀況，故動詞皆須用過去式。3.「我沒有發燒」為「因」，「我沒有去醫院」為「果」，故第一格填 because 或第二格填 so；because 與 so 皆為表達因果關係的連接詞，故不可用在同一句子中。4. 由後句為 because 作為開頭可知，前句應是問「為什麼」，故用疑問詞 why；且由文中敘述可知，作者並沒有去看醫生，故 (A) 不符合文意。

items.prompt: Doris：Did you watch the movie Wonder?Gina：No, I didn’t. Did you?Doris：Yes. I cried when I watched it. It was about a little boy, Auggie. Auggie had a different face.Gina：Did his classmates laugh at him?Doris：Yes, so his parents taught him at home, but they really worried about him. They wanted their son to make some friends, so they sent him to school when he was ten years old.Gina：What happened to him then?Doris：At first, no one wanted to be Auggie’s friend, so Auggie’s teacher asked his classmate Jack to take care of him. On the first day, Jack was afraid of Auggie, but they became friends after Jack found Auggie funny.Gina：How did their classmates treat them after that?Doris：They followed Jack and became friends with Auggie after they found out that he was kind. They knew more about Auggie when they talked to him.Gina：It is a wonderful story. I can’t wait to watch it. when 當……時 laugh at 取笑 funny 好笑的 after 在……之後 wonderful 美好的（ ）1. Why did Auggie’s parents teach him at home when he was little? (A) Because of his face. (B) Because of his parents’ work. (C) Because he couldn’t read or write. (D) Because he couldn’t walk to school.（ ）2. What happened after Jack and Auggie became friends? (A) Auggie’s teacher was afraid of them. (B) Their classmates started laughing at Jack, too. (C) Auggie’s parents were still worried about him. (D) Their classmates also became friends with Auggie. （ ）3. Which is NOT true about the movie Wonder? (A) Jack was afraid of Auggie until the end of the movie. (B) Auggie had a different face, but he was kind and funny. (C) Auggie’s parents sent him to school when he was ten years old. (D) Auggie’s classmates knew more about him when they talked to him.
choices: Because he couldn’t read or write.
Because he couldn’t walk to school.（ ）2. What happened after Jack and Auggie became friends?
Auggie’s teacher was afraid of them.
Their classmates started laughing at Jack, too.
Auggie’s parents were still worried about him.
Their classmates also became friends with Auggie. （ ）3. Which is NOT true about the movie Wonder?
Jack was afraid of Auggie until the end of the movie.
Auggie had a different face, but he was kind and funny.
Auggie’s parents sent him to school when he was ten years old.
Auggie’s classmates knew more about him when they talked to him.
items.explanation: 1. 由 Doris 回應可知，他去學校會被同學嘲笑，故他爸媽在家裡教他的原因，推知是因為 Auggie 的臉。2. 由對話可知，在 Jack 跟 Auggie 變成好朋友之後，其他同學也發現 Auggie 很善良，所以與他成為朋友。3. (A) Jack 只有第一天害怕 Auggie，他們後來變成好朋友了。

items.prompt: Dear Paula,When I first saw the photos of Zang Zang Bao on social media, my mouth was watering. Today I finally got a chance to have one. It was really delicious. After I ate it, my mouth was full of chocolate. The flavor and texture were great. Maybe we can eat Zang Zang Bao together next time.Susan------------------------------------------------------Dear Susan,You finally tried Zang Zang Bao. That was great. But how does it get so popular in Taiwan? Do you know that? Well, everything began in Korea. Many famous people there ate Zang Zang Bao and didn’t wipe their mouths right away. Then they took photos and uploaded them to social media. Because of these interesting photos, Zang Zang Bao got people’s attention. Many people in Korea stood in a long line for it. Later, a famous person in Taiwan did the same thing. She uploaded her photo of eating Zang Zang Bao to social media, and then many people were crazy about it, too. By the way, I have free time this Saturday afternoon. Why don’t we meet up at Jenny’s and wait in line to enjoy some Zang Zang Bao?Paula social media 社群媒體 chance 機會 be full of 充滿 chocolate 巧克力 flavor 口味 texture 口感 popular 受歡迎的 wipe 擦拭 interesting 有趣的 line 隊伍 crazy 著迷的（ ）1. What will you do when a person “gets your attention”? will 將會 (A) Give him or her up. (B) Get away from him or her. (C) Want to know about him or her. (D) Throw rocks at him or her.（ ）2. What do we know about the famous person in Taiwan from the second letter? (A) She made delicious Zang Zang Bao. (B) She worked with some famous people in Korea. (C) She stood in a long line for Zang Zang Bao. (D) She put her photo on social media after she ate Zang Zang Bao.（ ）3. Which is NOT true about Zang Zang Bao? (A) It got popular first in Taiwan. (B) You need chocolate when you make it. (C) People in Korea were crazy about it before it got popular in Taiwan. (D) Many famous people in Korea ate it, and they didn’t wipe their mouths before they took photos.（ ）4. What might be “Jenny’s”? (A) (B) (C) (D)
choices: Get away from him or her.
Want to know about him or her.
Throw rocks at him or her.（ ）2. What do we know about the famous person in Taiwan from the second letter?
She made delicious Zang Zang Bao.
She worked with some famous people in Korea.
She stood in a long line for Zang Zang Bao.
She put her photo on social media after she ate Zang Zang Bao.（ ）3. Which is NOT true about Zang Zang Bao?
It got popular first in Taiwan.
You need chocolate when you make it.
People in Korea were crazy about it before it got popular in Taiwan.
Many famous people in Korea ate it, and they didn’t wipe their mouths before they took photos.（ ）4. What might be “Jenny’s”?
items.explanation: 1. 由內文可知，人們在看過那些有趣的自拍照後，髒髒包便開始流行起來，可知 get people’s attention 是引起人們注意並且想要了解這個事物。2. 第二封信後面提到，臺灣名人在吃過髒髒包後，把照片放在社群媒體上，引發髒髒包在臺灣的流行。3. 由第二封信可知，髒髒包最早是在韓國受歡迎。4. 由上下文可知，髒髒包是一種巧克力麵包，故 Paula 和 Susan 應該約在咖啡廳。

items.prompt: Gratitude JournalWhyLearning from bad things is important, but sometimes we just think about the bad things, and not about the good things in our lives. It’s easy to take the good things and people in our lives for granted. Writing down these good thoughts in a gratitude journal helps people remember the good things in life. In fact, giving thanks for them can make you healthy and happy.How There is no wrong way to keep a gratitude journal, but here are some steps for you to start.1. Spend 15 minutes every day on your gratitude journal, at least three times a week for at least two weeks.2. Prepare a notebook and a pen.3. Think about this question, “Who / what can I thank?”4. Write down five answers. It is important to write—don’t just think about your answers in your head. The things you write can be very small (“I had a delicious sandwich for lunch today.”) or very big (“My aunt bought a new house.”).5. The goal of keeping a gratitude journal is to remember a good person or thing in your life—then enjoy the good emotions that come with it. gratitude journal感恩日記 take… for granted 認為……是理所當然的 remember 記得 make 使變成 spend 花費 at least 至少 notebook 筆記本 goal 目的 emotion 情緒（ ）1. What can a gratitude journal do? (A) It can help people forget bad dreams. (B) It can help people learn from bad things. (C) It can help people learn how to write fast. fast 迅速地 (D) It can help people remember good things in life.（ ）2. Who may need to keep a gratitude journal? (A) Ted. He always forgets to do his homework and makes his teacher angry. angry 生氣 (B) Lily. She always writes down bad things from people and is always sad. (C) Cindy. She remembers all the help from people and always gives thanks to them. (D) Sam. He loves helping people and is happy when others say “thank you” to him.（ ）3. What does “thought” mean in the reading? mean 意指 (A) Problem. (B) Story. (C) Idea. (D) Plan.
choices: It can help people forget bad dreams.
It can help people learn from bad things.
It can help people learn how to write fast. fast 迅速地

Ted. He always forgets to do his homework and makes his teacher angry. angry 生氣
Lily. She always writes down bad things from people and is always sad.
Cindy. She remembers all the help from people and always gives thanks to them.
Sam. He loves helping people and is happy when others say “thank you” to him.（ ）3. What does “thought” mean in the reading? mean 意指

Which is true about Vicky? (A) She doesn’t like London. (B) She doesn’t like rainy days. (C) She loves to walk in the rain. (D) She likes to stay at home on rainy days.（ ）3. Which is NOT true? (A) Ken likes the fall in London. (B) Robert doesn’t like cold weather. (C) Vicky enjoys rainy days in London. (D) In London, winter is the time to enjoy the beauty of leaves.
choices: Ken.（ ）2. Which is true about Vicky?
She loves to walk in the rain.
She likes to stay at home on rainy days.（ ）3. Which is NOT true?

Vicky enjoys rainy days in London.

items.prompt: Chuck：Good morning, Erica. __1.__Erica：What do you mean? It’s Monday, and I have a class at 9 a.m.Chuck：Didn’t you __2.__ last weekend?Erica：No, I didn’t have a cold. I just had a slight headache and a sore throat.Chuck：But didn’t that turn into a cold?Erica：Obviously not because I’m here and I’m fine now.Chuck：What’s your secret? __3.__Erica：I just __4.__ some medicine, __4.__ hot tea with lemon and honey, and slept all day at home.Chuck：Is that all?Erica：Oh yeah, I also ate some ice cream to treat my sore throat.Chuck：Ice cream for a sore throat? It’s so cool. Maybe I can try your way to treat my cold next time. mean 意指 slight 輕微的 turn into 轉變成 obviously 明顯地 secret 祕訣 lemon 檸檬 honey 蜂蜜（ ）1. (A) What date is today? (B) How are you doing? (C) When is your birthday? (D) Why are you here today?（ ）2. (A) catch a cold (B) come to school (C) visit my country (D) have history classes（ ）3. (A) I did that, too. (B) What did you do? (C) What was wrong? (D) Where were you?（ ）4. (A) ate; drank (B) eat; drink (C) took; drank (D) take; drink

Ryan Serhant 在實境秀中短時間內就賣掉許多房屋，還因為該節目而變得有名，更進一步成為另一個節目 Sell It Like Serhant 的主持人，可推知他在實境秀中相當成功。

In fact, women in the US make 82 cents for every dollar made by men. This is because women often work in fields that pay less. According to the American Association of University Women, male-dominated fields usually pay better, even when female-dominated fields need the same level of education and skill. So, as a Barbie fan, I have to say, Barbie has helped a lot to break through the glass ceiling, and she always shows that a woman has choices. entertainment 娛樂 chef 主廚 male-dominated field 男性主導的領域 likely 可能地 outperform 勝過 according to 根據 female 女性 education 教育 skill 技巧 glass ceiling 無形限制（ ）1. According to the infographic, which is true? infographic 圖解資訊 (A) Nearly half of Barbie’s jobs are in Sports. (B) Fewer than 10% of Barbie’s jobs are teachers. (C) Fewer than 5% of Barbie’s jobs are engineers. (D) More than 30% of Barbie’s jobs are in Entertainment Business.（ ）2. What is the best title for the reading? This helps people have a healthier and better relationship with social media. Besides, the RSPH asked the public what they believe are the most toxic elements of social media. The toxic elements of social media are:1. The “like” button2. Push notifications3. Fear of Missing Out (FOMO)4. Pressure from influencers ? items.prompt: I had a really bad day yesterday. First, I was woken up by a loud noise outside my window. It was really scary. I couldn’t go back to sleep after that, so I got up and got ready for school. When I went to put on my uniform, I noticed it smelled because I forgot to wash it. I didn’t have another one, so I had no choice but to wear it. Then when I got on the bus, all the seats were taken, so I had to stand all the way to school. Things just got worse there. I was made fun of because of my clothes, but I didn’t feel it was a laughing matter. Also, I was made to sit away from the other students, and I wasn’t picked for any teams. Lastly, before I was allowed to go home, I was told not to let it happen again. At that moment, I realized it’s really important to wear clean clothes, isn’t it? realize 意識到（ ）1. What happened to the writer? (A) He was woken up by his mom. (B) He wasn’t allowed to go home. (C) He was told to sit down on the bus. (D) He was made to wear his smelly uniform.（ ）2. What does “made fun of” mean? (A) Laughed at. (B) Expected to. (C) Held onto. (D) Covered with.（ ）3. Why WASN’T the writer picked to be on a team? (A) He wasn’t feeling well. (B) He didn’t wear a uniform. (C) He wasn’t a very good player. (D) His clothes smelled really bad.
choices: He was woken up by his mom.
He wasn’t allowed to go home.
He was told to sit down on the bus.
He was made to wear his smelly uniform.（ ）2. What does “made fun of” mean?
Covered with.（ ）3. Why WASN’T the writer picked to be on a team?
He wasn’t a very good player.
items.explanation: 1. 由第五到第六句可知，因為忘了洗制服，只好穿上有臭味的制服。2. 由上下文可知，作者因為制服有臭味而被「嘲笑」，所以做事都不順利。3. 由倒數第三到第四句可知，作者因為制服有臭味而沒有被選入隊伍。

Anyway, I just found out ＿2.＿ they are going to open a Purplebottle café in our neighborhood soon. Isn’t that great?Marcus：Um, what are you talking about? And why are you interested in a purple bottle?Brittany：No, silly. I’m not interested in a purple-colored bottle. At Purplebottle, the clerks slowly pour hot water over the ground coffee beans, and they let it drip down little by little into a cup.Marcus：＿5.＿ Besides, I think that’s going to take a long time for one little cup of coffee. lottery 彩券 neighborhood 社區 pour 倒 ground coffee 研磨咖啡 drip down 滴下（ ）1. items.prompt: You can do a great deal with money. It can help you in many ways, and you can use it to make many difficult problems go away. With it, you can also buy nice things for yourself and for others. In some cases, it could even save your life. But, give the matter some thought, and you’ll soon understand something important about money: It can’t buy everything. In fact, many of life’s most wonderful things don’t cost a cent. Take sleep, for example. Even the richest person on Earth can’t buy a good night’s rest. Of course, you can buy a comfortable bed, but this still doesn’t mean you’ll sleep well. You need to get enough exercise and be in the right state of mind to sleep. If you’re sad, nervous about the next day, or worried about a loved one, not all the money in the world can bring you a natural, sound sleep and sweet dreams. Another thing money can’t get you—and this is no joke—is laughter. You won’t, after all, see a sense of humor in any department stores or on the Internet. You can’t buy it in any markets or supermarkets, either. It’s a gift from the gods. For, rich or poor, life just isn’t worth living without laughing. If you think money can buy you love, a happy heart, an open mind, wise friends, family, health, hard work, knowledge, understanding, and life itself, you’re quite crazy, too. In other words, … give something some thought 認真思考 state 狀態 nervous 緊張的 laughter 笑 sense of humor 幽默感 worth 值得的（ ）1. Which of the following would be a good title for this reading? (A) Money Talks (B) Money Isn’t Everything (C) Money Doesn’t Grow on Trees (D) Money Makes the World Go Round( ) 2. Which of the following best describes the word “ sound”? describe 描述 (A) sound (adj.) “deep and peaceful” peaceful 和平的 (B) sound (n.) “something you can hear” (C) sound (adj.) “something you can believe in” (D) sound (v.) “to make a sound or noise”( ) 3. According to the reading, which of the following is NOT an example that money can’t buy? according to 根據 (A) Love. (B) Laughter. (C) A good night’s sleep. (D) A comfortable bed.
items.explanation: 1. 由第一段可知，文章主要在敘述金錢買不到所有的事物，故選 (B)。2. 將四個選項帶入可推知，sound 在此表 (A)。3. 由文中舉例兩項金錢買不到的事物——睡眠及歡笑，可推知，金錢買不到的東西為 (D)。

items.prompt: A study by the Child Welfare League Foundation showed that teenagers aged 13 to 15 worried most about their schoolwork, their friends, and their appearance. Schoolwork was their biggest worry. Up to 60% of the teenagers said their grades were not good enough. As for friends, they worried about fighting with friends, being different from others, and feeling uncomfortable about the nicknames their friends gave them. Besides, the study showed that about 20% of the teenagers didn’t like how they looked and wished they could change their appearance. However, even though teenagers had many worries, about 33% of them would keep their problems to themselves instead of telling anyone. That’s why we set up a helpline for teenagers. We want troubled teenagers to call the helpline and we’re always here to listen…＊helpline 電話服務熱線 Child Welfare League Foundation 兒福聯盟基金會 nickname 綽號（ ）1. Which best fits in the blank? blank 空格 (A) you failed to become a doctor (B) someone tricked you out of money (C) you want to tell us your successful story (D) you don’t know how to get along with your classmates（ ）2. What does “appearance” mean? (A) The way a person lives. (B) The way a person talks. (C) The way a person looks. (D) The way a person thinks.（ ）3. Why do they have a helpline for teenagers? (A) Because teenagers are always fighting at school. (B) Because teenagers need help with their schoolwork. (C) Because teenagers like to share their school days. (D) Because many teenagers keep their problems to themselves.
choices: you failed to become a doctor
someone tricked you out of money
you want to tell us your successful story
you don’t know how to get along with your classmates（ ）2. What does “appearance” mean?
The way a person thinks.（ ）3. Why do they have a helpline for teenagers?
Because teenagers are always fighting at school.

items.explanation: 1. 根據文章，青少年的三大煩惱：學業、人際關係、外貌。故可推知此處應選與其相關的 (D)，不知如何與同學相處。2. 文章列出青少年的三大煩惱後，便逐一深入說明。文章第一段最後提到 20% 的青少年不喜歡自己看起來的樣子，故可知此處應選 (C)。3. 由文章第二段第一、二句，33% 的青少年不會告訴他人自己遇到的問題，因此兒福聯盟設立此專線，故可知此處應選 (D)。

items.prompt: A：Do you mind ＿＿＿ the windows? It’s hot in here.B：＿＿＿, I do. The noise outside is too loud.(A) open; Yes (B) opening; Yes (C) open; No (D) opening; No
items.explanation: mind 當動詞時，意為「介意」，其後方須接動名詞（V-ing）。由句意，A 問 B「你會介意開窗戶嗎？」，B 回答「外面的噪音太吵了。」，可知 B 拒絕 A 的請求，故其回答應為 Yes, I do.（「會，我介意。」）

items.source: 康軒 / 115上康軒國中英語題庫 / Database / Examine.mdb
items.subject: 英文
items.prompt: After I talked to my new neighbor ＿＿＿ across from me, I found out that she was the actress ＿＿＿! I can’t wait to tell my brother about this.(A) lives; my brother likes her(B) that lives; my brother likes(C) lives; my brother likes(D) that lives; my brother likes her
choices: that lives; my brother likes her
items.explanation: 前句關係子句的先行詞 neighbor 為人，且為主詞，故關係代名詞須使用 that 或 who，且不可省略；後句的關係子句的先行詞 actress 為人，且為受詞，故關係代名詞須使用 that 或 who，亦或省略，並且後方不須再搭配第二個受詞 her。

items.subject: 英文
items.prompt: Picture that you are walking on the street. Suddenly, you trip. You stand up right away because you think everyone is watching you. Later, you find out that nobody actually noticed. Does this sound familiar to you? If so, you’re not alone. This is what social psychologists call the spotlight effect. It explains why people always believe many people are watching them. However, people are not paying as much attention to you as they are to themselves. The spotlight effect can limit your ability and make you worry too much. Here are some ways to overcome the spotlight effect. One way is to remember that people are not paying as much attention to you as you think. If you trip or spill something by mistake, chances are that few people actually notice. Also, pay attention to others. By doing so, you’ll think more about others and their ideas, not yourself…* social psychologist 社會心理學家 spotlight effect 聚光燈效應 familiar 熟悉的 attention 注意 limit 限制 ability 能力 overcome 克服 spill 灑出（ ）1. What’s the purpose of the reading? purpose 目的 (A) To tell people how to make fewer mistakes. (B) To tell people how to get everyone’s attention. (C) To tell people how to overcome the spotlight effect. (D) To tell people how to stay away from being noticed.（ ）2. Jane feels interested in the spotlight effect and wants to know more. Which of the following is NOT an example of the spotlight effect? (A) As you walk past several people, you can feel everyone looking at you. (B) Today is your first day of work, and you think everyone is looking at the spot on your shirt. spot 汙漬 (C) In a group meeting, you feel like everyone in the group is judging every word you say. judge 批評 (D) When you worry about how you look, others also experience the spotlight effect and think about their looks.
choices: To tell people how to make fewer mistakes.
To tell people how to get everyone’s attention.
To tell people how to overcome the spotlight effect.
To tell people how to stay away from being noticed.（ ）2. Jane feels interested in the spotlight effect and wants to know more. Which of the following is NOT an example of the spotlight effect?
As you walk past several people, you can feel everyone looking at you.
Today is your first day of work, and you think everyone is looking at the spot on your shirt. spot 汙漬
In a group meeting, you feel like everyone in the group is judging every word you say. judge 批評
When you worry about how you look, others also experience the spotlight effect and think about their looks.
items.explanation: 1. 全文可分為兩部分：何謂聚光燈效應以及如何克服它。2. 選項 (A)、(B)、(C) 皆為「過度在意他人眼光、以為自己被注視」的心理狀態，符合聚光燈效應；(D) 則是說明「他人也都在關注他們自己」的客觀現象，並非聚光燈效應的情境範例，故選 (D)。

items.prompt: Dear Green Connections,I love Car Free Day, and I’d like to share how I celebrate it with you and your readers.Car Free Day is a day that I take very seriously because it is very important not only to us but also to our planet. First, I must tell you that before I learned about this special day, I drove my car everywhere. Sadly, I even drove to places that were less than five minutes away on foot. I now know that was a bad idea. However, all that has changed. On Car Free Day and all the other days of the year, I ride my bike to places I need to go. At first, it was very hard for me to get to the places far from my house because I was not in good shape and got tired really easily. Then, little by little, I got stronger and could go to places many miles away. Now, there isn’t a day that I don’t ride my bike.Biking has truly helped me see the world in a new way. What’s more, I can’t imagine going back to a life that wasn’t good for me or the Earth.All the best,Derek imagine 想像（ ）1. What is the purpose of this letter? purpose 目的 (A) To explain a new way to get around quickly. (B) To share a story about cars with a group of readers. (C) To tell a bike company their bikes were poorly made. (D) To share how biking changed his life and helped the Earth.（ ）2. Which is true about Derek before he knew about Car Free Day? (A) He walked to many places. (B) He rode his bike everywhere. (C) He stayed at home most days. (D) He drove his car to many places.（ ）3. How does Derek feel about biking? (A) It changed his life. (B) It’s nothing special. (C) It doesn’t help him or the planet. (D) It’s not only tiring but also boring.
choices: To explain a new way to get around quickly.
To share a story about cars with a group of readers.
To tell a bike company their bikes were poorly made.
To share how biking changed his life and helped the Earth.（ ）2. Which is true about Derek before he knew about Car Free Day?
He stayed at home most days.
He drove his car to many places.（ ）3. How does Derek feel about biking?
It doesn’t help him or the planet.
It’s not only tiring but also boring.
items.explanation: 1. 此文章為作者分享自己從開車改成騎腳踏車，並說明這樣對自己和地球都有幫助。2. 由第二段可知，作者以前不管要去的地方是遠或近，都是開車去。3. 由文章最後可知，騎單車改變了作者的生活方式。

items.prompt: 【B5L6素養題】 Whether you are shopping at a supermarket or at a clothing store, many of the prices ＿1.＿ you see usually have something in common. Prices are more likely to end in .99 more than any other pair of numbers. Why aren’t prices just even numbers? Many stores like to mark their prices to end in .99 for discounts, and customers almost never notice that ＿2.＿. Though no one really knows who or how the trick started, it has been around for at least a century. Ending a price in .99 is based on the theory: We read from left to right, so we usually only see the first number of the price. The price ＿3.＿ starts with a 4 appears to be a better deal than the one that starts with 5. That’s why even though a product for $4.99 may be just one cent cheaper, the trick always helps sell more. ＿4.＿, the .99 alone allows people to believe that the item is on sale. Customers often think they are getting a good deal when they buy something with a price ending in .99. The trick doesn’t only work for cents. In other studies about women’s clothes, a dress ＿5.＿ price is changed from $34 to $39 sells more. However, changing it from $34 to $44 doesn’t have much different results. This proves that the number 9 has a surprising effect on customers. Now you know the secrets behind the prices. Look at them wisely when you go shopping next time. even 偶數的 be based on 以……為根據 theory 理論 prove 證明 effect 影響（ ）1. (A) who (B) what (C) whose (D) ╳（ ）2. (A) they are fooled (B) tricks are expected (C) deals can’t be passed up (D) products are hard to be reached（ ）3. (A) what (B) which (C) whose (D) ╳（ ）4. (A) However (B) Therefore (C) What’s more (D) As you can see（ ）5. (A) which (B) whose (C) that (D) who
choices: products are hard to be reached（ ）3.
items.explanation: 1. 當先行詞為關係子句的受詞時，關係代名詞用 which / that 或省略。2. 由後句「雖然沒有人真的知道這個陷阱是如何開始」，可推斷顧客幾乎沒注意到「他們被愚弄了」。3. 先行詞 the price 為物，關係代名詞用 which 或 that。4. 由前句「這就是為什麼即使一個只是便宜一分錢的 $4.99 產品，但這陷阱總是賣出更多產品。」和後句「.99 讓人們相信這物品在特價」，可推斷這裡是用「而且；此外」來做補充說明。5. whose 是關係代名詞的所有格，須置於關係子句的句首，結構為「先行詞＋whose＋名詞」。

items.prompt: 【B5L4素養題】 Building your vocabulary is one of the key points for mastering a language. However, building vocabulary is more than just knowing words. Here are some right ways to learn words. First, you should use the words you learn more often. The best way to build vocabulary is to be an active learner. Here are the steps to become one: to learn ten new words every day, to write them down in a diary, and to use them in conversation. When you use as many new words as you can in real life, you can easily memorize them. Second, it is also good to learn words in small groups. By doing this, you can master a language in a more systematic way. There aren’t really any shortcuts to learning words. To have a wide and large vocabulary, you need time and have to practice in the right ways. For example, some roots of English words come from Latin（拉丁）or Greek（希臘）, and to learn these words, it’s better to know how they are formed first. The more you know a word, the better you can memorize and use it. Third, to build your vocabulary, you should always keep in mind that it is worth doing. Reading out the words or writing them down may sometimes be boring to you, so try to practice them with what you like. vocabulary 字彙 master 精通 active 主動的 conversation 對話 memorize 記憶 systematic 系統化的 shortcut 捷徑 wide 廣泛的 root 字根 worth 值得（ ）1. What does “them” mean? (A) The houses someone built. (B) The learners someone met. (C) The words someone learned. (D) The languages someone mastered.（ ）2. Which might be the best title for the reading? title 標題 (A) How to Read English Stories Easily (B) Good Ways to Learn More New Words (C) Ways to Improve Your Writing Skills improve 改進 (D) English: The Most Widely Used Language in the World widely 廣泛地（ ）3. Which is NOT true about the reading? (A) It is not easy to keep learning new words. (B) There is no need to learn new words in a systematic way. (C) When you learn a word, you should use it to keep it yours. (D) Some English words and Latin words have something in common.
choices: The languages someone mastered.（ ）2. Which might be the best title for the reading? title 標題
How to Read English Stories Easily
Good Ways to Learn More New Words
Ways to Improve Your Writing Skills improve 改進
English: The Most Widely Used Language in the World widely 廣泛地（ ）3. Which is NOT true about the reading?
It is not easy to keep learning new words.
There is no need to learn new words in a systematic way.

items.explanation: 1. 由前句提到每天學十個新字可知，them 在此指學過的字。2. 由第一段最後一句可知，本文主旨為學習更多新字的好方法。3. 由第三段可知，利用字根學習可更有系統地精通語言。

items.prompt: 【B5L1素養題】 Hi, everyone. Before we learn how to make this delicious snack, let’s talk about the history of croissants. My grandma used to bake croissants for the family all the time. I always thought they were French, but they were actually from Austria（奧地利）. In 1683, Austria was at war with the Ottoman Turks（奧圖曼土耳其人）. One evening, some Austrian bakers heard the Turks digging a tunnel under the city. They quickly told the soldiers, so they could get ready and save the city. To celebrate their success, the bakers created a special treat—croissant. Croissants are made of flour and lots of butter. They have been mostly in the shape of a crescent since they were created. Because a crescent was a symbol on the flags of Ottoman Turks, the bakers decided to bake croissants in this shape. I’ve shared my popular recipe with many people since I started teaching. However, if you are interested in learning more about croissants and my recipe, don’t miss my upcoming baking class! croissant 可頌 tunnel 地道 success 成功 create 創造 crescent 新月 symbol 象徵 flag 旗幟 recipe 食譜 interested 感興趣的 upcoming 即將到來的 discount 折扣 location 位置（ ）1. What’s the purpose of the reading? purpose 目的 (A) To keep notes of a family recipe. (B) To celebrate the birthday of a country. (C) To invite people to the cooking class. (D) To show what we need for making croissants.（ ）2. Which of the following might be the flag of Ottoman Turks? (A) (B) (C) (D) （ ）3. Which is NOT true according to the reading? according to 根據 (A) Croissants have been popular for hundreds of years. (B) The writer’s grandma learned to make croissants in 1683. (C) Old students of the writer can pay less for the baking class. (D) Austrians celebrated with croissants in 1683 because they won the war.
choices: To keep notes of a family recipe.
To celebrate the birthday of a country.

items.prompt: 【B5L4素養題】 Oxford English Dictionary (OED) often adds new words to the book. Some of these new words are created when two words are put together. One example of this is “voluntourism,” which combines the words “volunteer” and “tourism.” It means you work as a volunteer when you are on a trip. In other words, it is not just to have a vacation. Instead, it is a chance for volunteers to use their skills and interests to help others in need. Every year, many people from rich countries travel to poor countries and hope to do some good. This has been popular for almost half of a century, and it was finally added to the dictionary in 2014. On the other hand, “staycation” was added to OED in 2010 after it became widely popular in the late 2000s. The earliest use of the word was back in 2003 when a reporter combined “ A ” and “ B ” together. People or families usually stay home and enjoy activities or plan a day trip around their house during their staycation. From swimming in the backyard, visiting a museum, to going to local festivals, these help create the feeling of a vacation without going abroad. After COVID-19 hit the world in 2020, people were not sure if the place they visited was safe. Therefore, the idea of staycation was brought back again. volunteer 自願；志工 tourism 旅遊業 skill 技能 travel 旅遊 widely 廣泛地 activity 活動 backyard 後院 feeling 感覺（ ）1. What might “ A ” and “ B ” in the reading be? (A) House; activity (B) Stand; location (C) Stay; vacation (D) Home; holiday（ ）2. Why did staycation become popular again in 2020? (A) People wanted to take action to help. (B) People found pleasure in it by accident. (C) People didn’t know if it was safe to travel. (D) People tried to put themselves in others’ shoes.（ ）3. Which is NOT true? (A) Voluntourism became popular mostly in richer countries. (B) People enjoy doing nothing at home during their staycation. (C) One way new words are created is by combining two words. (D) New words are usually found in dictionaries after they are popular.
choices: Home; holiday（ ）2. Why did staycation become popular again in 2020?
People wanted to take action to help.
People found pleasure in it by accident.
People didn’t know if it was safe to travel.
People tried to put themselves in others’ shoes.（ ）3. Which is NOT true?
Voluntourism became popular mostly in richer countries.
People enjoy doing nothing at home during their staycation.
One way new words are created is by combining two words.
New words are usually found in dictionaries after they are popular.
items.explanation: 1. 由第一段 voluntourism 舉例可知，組新字的原則為分別取兩個字的一部分，並合併字義成新字，故僅選項 (C) 合理。2. 因 2020 年 COVID-19 侵襲全球，人們不確定去哪裡旅遊是安全的，故 staycation 又開始受歡迎。3. 由第二段可知，staycation 包含室內活動，甚至是前往家附近的博物館或節慶等，並非在家無事可做。

items.prompt: Pop culture is all around us. We listen to pop music and watch movies every day. These things are fun. However, they also teach us about gender. Sometimes, they use “stereotypes.” These are common ideas about how boys and girls should act. In many pop songs, men have to be strong. They do not show their feelings. On the other hand, women are often not strong and sometimes afraid. In the song’s words, women often need help from men. These are stereotypes. Actually, boys can be sensitive, and girls can be brave and strong. Old movies also show these stereotypes. In these movies, women often stay at home. They cook and clean for the family. Men go out to work. They are the successful people in the stories. Because of these stories, some people believe girls cannot be successful in life. But this is not true. Today, many things have changed. We see “girl power” in many new movies and the women are strong and successful. We also hear songs about men. These men share their feelings. It is important to think about the ideas in pop culture. Do not let movies or songs change you. You can be yourself! feeling 感情 pop culture 流行文化（ ）1. What is the reading mainly about? (A) Pop music is much better than old movies. (B) Only men can be successful in popular movies today. (C) Pop culture can give people wrong ideas about gender. (D) Most girls like to stay at home and cook for their family.（ ）2. What does the word “sensitive” mean in the second paragraph? paragraph 段落 (A) Being mad at other people. (B) Having a very strong body. (C) Working very hard in a big company. (D) Showing and talking about how you feel.（ ）3. What do women often do in many old movies? (A) They have very successful lives. (B) They help men share their feelings. (C) They go out to work in big companies. (D) They take care of the home and cook for the family.
choices: Pop music is much better than old movies.
Only men can be successful in popular movies today.
Pop culture can give people wrong ideas about gender.
Most girls like to stay at home and cook for their family.（ ）2. What does the word “sensitive” mean in the second paragraph? paragraph 段落
Working very hard in a big company.
Showing and talking about how you feel.（ ）3. What do women often do in many old movies?
They help men share their feelings.
They go out to work in big companies.
They take care of the home and cook for the family.
items.explanation: 1. 綜觀全文，分析了歌曲與電影如何傳遞這些可能錯誤的訊息，並在結尾呼籲讀者要做自己，故選 (C)。2. 由第二段描述男人不表現情感，隨後反駁說男孩其實也可以很 sensitive 可知，呈現前後對比。因此，sensitive 指的是展現並談論自己的感受，故選 (D)。3. 由第三段第二句跟第三句「女性經常待在家，為家人烹飪與打掃」可知，應選 (D)。

items.unit: L6_Are You One of the Customers Who Companies Trick？
items.prompt: 填入正確的動詞形式：1. The notebook computer that was bought by my grandfather ＿＿＿＿＿＿ (appear) to be broken.2. The fish that ＿＿＿＿＿＿ (catch) by those fishermen were big.3. The boys that ＿＿＿＿＿＿ (play) basketball on the basketball court now are tall and strong.

items.prompt: Well-known in all four corners of the planet is the story of the lost city of Atlantis. It ＿1.＿ by Plato in Greece around 360 BC. The place was said to be a group of islands, and it ＿2.＿ by special people. Atlantis had a great society with good and smart people, and they were said to have lived a perfect life. Expensive things were enjoyed by everyone, and the beautiful world was shared with lots of plants and animals. It was almost too good to be true. In truth, though, the perfect people were not perfect at all. They never had enough and always wanted more. They fought each other over stupid things. Most importantly, they could no longer tell between right and wrong. All this was seen by the gods, and seeing the people of Atlantis losing their way made them angry. As punishment, ＿3.＿. It ended up dropping all the way down to the bottom of the ocean because of them. To this day, many people believe Atlantis was real ＿4.＿ it’s just a story. Some people have even tried everything possible to find the lost city. society 社會 plant 植物 too... to 太……而不能 in truth 事實上 god 神 punishment 處罰（ ）1. (A) was first told (B) first told was (C) has first told (D) is telling first（ ）2. (A) was made (B) made to be (C) was making (D) has been made（ ）3. (A) fire was burned on the gods (B) the city was filled with love (C) the city was hit by fire and earthquakes (D) the people were moved to a bigger and better city（ ）4. (A) so (B) because (C) than (D) although
choices: fire was burned on the gods
the city was filled with love
the city was hit by fire and earthquakes
the people were moved to a bigger and better city（ ）4.
items.explanation: 1. 由前句可知 it 指 the story；而故事是「被講述」，用被動語態。2. 由 it 當主詞，且講述過去的故事，故用過去式被動語態。3. 由前句可知眾神對 Atlantis 人的所作所為非常生氣，所以要給他們處罰，故此句應為「這城巿被火和地震襲擊」。4. 由於連接的前後兩句文意完全相反，應用代表文意轉折的連接詞 although。

items.prompt: In Taiwan, there is a big problem with a green animal called the iguana. This animal is not from Taiwan. People brought iguanas to Taiwan as pets many years ago. But some people let their iguanas go outside when they did not want them anymore. The iguanas like warm weather, and many places in Taiwan have good weather and food for them. Because of this, the number of iguanas grew very fast. Iguanas eat many plants and vegetables that farmers grow. This causes a big problem for farmers because they lose food and money. The iguanas also hurt some small animals that live in the wild. Iguanas can live for about 20 years, and female iguanas lay many eggs, around 80 eggs at one time. This means that the number of iguanas can grow quickly. Now, there are about 200,000 iguanas in Taiwan. Most of them live in the south and middle parts of Taiwan, near farms and cities. The government knows this problem is serious. They made a plan to catch and remove many iguanas from nature. The government made teams of hunters and trained many people to catch iguanas. They also give money as a prize to people who catch big iguanas. This year, the government plans to catch more than 100,000 iguanas. They set up four teams of indigenous hunters and nine local teams to find and catch the iguanas. The government also made an app for farmers and hunters to report where they see iguanas. This helps catch more iguanas quickly. The government also works to stop people from bringing iguanas to Taiwan or letting pets go outside. This problem shows us that we must be careful with pets and nature. We should not let animals hurt the plants and animals that live in Taiwan. If we protect nature well, Taiwan will be a better home for all animals, plants, and people. We hope more people will help stop the iguana problem. Together, we can take care of our country and keep it beautiful and safe for the future. iguana 綠鬣蜥 plant 植物 cause 引起 wild 野外 female 母的 lay 產卵 government 政府 remove 除去 hunter 獵人 prize 獎品 indigenous 本土的（ ）1. According to the reading, how many eggs can a female iguana lay at one time? according to 根據 (A) 20 eggs. (B) 80 eggs. (C) 100,000 eggs. (D) About 200,000 eggs.（ ）2. What is the main reason why the number of iguanas grew so quickly in Taiwan? (A) Iguanas can fly well. (B) People brought them as food. (C) The government gave them money. (D) They were freed and found a good environment to live in. environment 環境（ ）3. If a farmer sees a big iguana on their farm, what is the best thing to do? (A) Scare it away. (B) Keep it as a pet. (C) Leave it alone and hope it goes away. alone 獨自的 (D) Use the government’s app to report where the iguana is.
choices: About 200,000 eggs.（ ）2. What is the main reason why the number of iguanas grew so quickly in Taiwan?
They were freed and found a good environment to live in. environment 環境（ ）3. If a farmer sees a big iguana on their farm, what is the best thing to do?
Leave it alone and hope it goes away. alone 獨自的
Use the government’s app to report where the iguana is.
items.explanation: 1. 由第二段第四句可知，母的綠鬣蜥一次可產八十顆卵，故選 (B)。2. 第一段提到綠鬣蜥數量增長的兩個關鍵：首先是人為因素（people let their iguanas go outside），其次是環境因素（good weather and food for them）。僅選項 (D) 符合這兩個因素。3. 由第三段可知，政府利用應用程式讓獵人或農夫回報看見綠鬣蜥的位置。因此，最正確且安全的作法是 (D) 使用政府的 app 回報位置。

items.prompt: Blythe Jones is back. The writer of the popular series on witches has written a new book, and it’s going to hit bookstores this spring. In The Dark Well, Jones continues Penelope’s story. The young witch lives in Salem, Massachusetts in the 21st century. She is tired of all the questions about her powers, so she tries to live a quiet and boring life. One day, she gets a surprise visitor. He is a reporter from Boston and is tracking down a story. He thinks the piece of news is really interesting, and it has led him right to Penelope’s door. However, she thinks he’s strange and isn’t interested in helping him. The reporter doesn’t give up, and after some time, he gets her to agree. When the young man starts digging up information about the scary dark well in her garden, things take a surprising turn. Although I like Jones’ other books, this new one is quite boring. It takes too long for the reporter to find Penelope and even longer to get her help. Also, it’s not surprising to see them become lovers because that kind of thing has happened many times in the series before. Besides, no one in their right mind would believe that two people would fall in love because of a dark well. series 系列 witch 女巫 continue 繼續 track down 追蹤 well 井（ ）1. To talk about a new piece of written work.

He / She didn’t want it to end.

Below is the video. nearly 幾乎 below 在下面 gun 槍 war 戰爭 try out 參加選拔 softball 壘球 swing 揮棒 honey 親愛的 hero 英雄（ ）1. Which is true about the people in the video? (A) One of them is Scott’s parent. (B) One of them is Scott’s brother. (C) One of them is the Big Hero’s sister. (D) One of them is the father of two of the others.（ ）2. What does Scott do for a living? (A) (B) (C) (D)
