items.prompt: Carol：Hey, Vincent. ＿1.＿Vincent：Do you mean the one ＿2.＿ Eric is talking to?Carol：Yes.Vincent：That’s Alice, the one ＿3.＿ many boys at school were crazy about.Carol：＿4.＿ I don’t remember her. Why is she here at our class reunion?Vincent：She was in Class 801, and she’s Eric’s girlfriend now.Carol：I see. class reunion 同學會（ ）1. (A) Are you looking for a new job? (B) How long have you known Eric? (C) Can you tell me why they are here? (D) Who’s the tall girl with long straight hair?（ ）2. (A) who (B) which (C) she (D) whose（ ）3. (A) which (B) what (C) that (D) she（ ）4. (A) She wasn’t our classmate, right? (B) Come to think of it, she really was. (C) Can I buy the item? (D) It sounds like a trick. Don’t fool me.
choices: Are you looking for a new job?
How long have you known Eric?
Can you tell me why they are here?
Who’s the tall girl with long straight hair?（ ）2.
Come to think of it, she really was.
It sounds like a trick. Don’t fool me.
items.explanation: 1. 由下句「你是指 Eric 正在交談的那位嗎？」可知，Carol 應該是詢問 Vincent 一位她不認識的人。2. 先行詞 the one 指人，關係代名詞用 who 或 that。3. 先行詞 the one 指 Alice，關係代名詞用 who 或 that。4. 由下文「我不記得她。而且她怎麼會出現在我們的同學會？」可知，Carol 在質疑 Alice 的身分。

items.prompt: Mr. Buffer was anything but poor. In fact, he was the richest man in the country. He had a young son ＿1.＿ name was Richie. One day, he decided to show him something to teach him about the world. Mr. Buffer wanted Richie to know how lucky he was to grow up in such a rich family, so he took him to see how people ＿2.＿ very little money lived. They left the city ＿3.＿ and spent several days visiting farms in the country before going back. On their way home, Mr. Buffer asked Richie what he saw and learned during the trip. His son thought everything was amazing. He saw that the people had lots of pets, but he just had one. He also found that the people had dozens of big ponds, but he only had a small one in his garden. He liked how they grew their food instead of having to buy it. He was also surprised that they could make friends with anyone without high walls. ＿4.＿ Then he thanked his dad for showing him how poor they were. anything but 絕不是（ ）1. (A) that (B) who (C) whose (D) his（ ）2. (A) have (B) in (C) about (D) with（ ）3. (A) knowledge (B) center (C) club (D) fair（ ）4. (A) He made a mark in his life. (B) The father was happy to hear that. (C) He said he learned many things and grew wiser. (D) They knew everything about building a pond themselves.
choices: He made a mark in his life.
The father was happy to hear that.
He said he learned many things and grew wiser.
They knew everything about building a pond themselves.
items.explanation: 1. 先行詞為 a young son，後方為名詞 name，故此處應使用關代所有格 whose。2. 表「有」的介系詞須用「with」。3. 由他們待在鄉村農場好幾天可知他們離開了市「中心」。4. 空格前說明 Richie 的所見所聞，可知「他說自己學到許多事情並增長見聞」。

items.prompt: Many students worry about money. They want to buy food, clothes, and fun things, but their money runs out too fast. This problem is common at school and in daily life. There are three simple tips that can help students who want to save money. They are: cutting small treats, making wise choices, and waiting before buying. Small treats seem cheap, but they add up quickly. Buying a breakfast sandwich, snacks, or bubble milk tea every day can cost a lot in one month. If you make these treats at home or buy them less often, you can save money. These small changes can mean more money in your pocket over time. Many people think the cheapest item is the best choice, but this is not always true. Very cheap things may break easily, and that means you’ll need to get another one again soon. Paying a little more for a good product can save money later. It can also cut down on waste and worries. When you see something you want, do not buy it right away. Wait for one or two days. During this time, ask yourself if you really need it. Often, the strong need to buy it will go away. This simple habit can stop you from buying things without thinking and keep your money safe. Saving money does not need to be hard. Small and good habits can make it easier. Which tip will you try this week to help your money last longer? daily 日常的 seem 似乎 bubble milk tea 珍珠奶茶（ ）1. What does the word “It” refer to? refer to 意指 (A) A cheap thing that breaks easily. (B) Getting another new item again soon. (C) Paying a little more for a good product. (D) The waste and worries in our daily life.（ ）2. Why does the writer tell students to “wait for one or two days” before buying something? (A) To wait for the shop to give a special discount. (B) To see if you really need the item, not just want it. (C) To give you enough time to ask your friends for their advice. advice 建議 (D) To make sure you have saved enough money in your pocket first.（ ）3. What is the reading mainly about? (A) Good sides of buying cheap items. (B) Good ways for students to save money. (C) The best way to make delicious snacks. (D) The best places to buy clothes and food.
choices: A cheap thing that breaks easily.
Getting another new item again soon.
Paying a little more for a good product.
The waste and worries in our daily life.（ ）2. Why does the writer tell students to “wait for one or two days” before buying something?
To wait for the shop to give a special discount.
To see if you really need the item, not just want it.
To give you enough time to ask your friends for their advice. advice 建議
To make sure you have saved enough money in your pocket first.（ ）3. What is the reading mainly about?
Good sides of buying cheap items.
Good ways for students to save money.
The best way to make delicious snacks.
The best places to buy clothes and food.
items.explanation: 1. It 指的是前一句「花多一點錢買好的產品」這件事，故應選 (C)。2. 由第四段第三句「在此期間，問自己是否真的需要它。」可知為辨認「需要與想要」，故應選(B)。3.文章開頭提及「三種省錢小提示」，故主要內容是關於學生如何省錢，可知應選 (B)。

items.prompt: Since the 1920s, the Oscars have been Hollywood’s most important events, and winning an Oscar has been a dream for everyone in the movie industry. The movie itself is not the only reason for winning an Oscar. The producers spend a lot of time going to parties and holding previews. Asking reporters to write about their movies costs a lot of money, too. Is winning an Oscar really worth all that hard work and money? Almost all the movies become successful after they are nominated for Best Picture. Because of the news, more and more people will notice those movies and be interested in them. Take Birdman, the Best Picture winner in 2015, for example. After its nomination, its box office sales suddenly grew 132%. However, its sales grew less than 8% after it won the Oscar. That still made people believe it was truly a good movie. Though some think the Oscars don’t choose the real best picture of the year anymore, most movie makers will keep working hard for that title to win at the box office. event 事件 industry 產業 reason 理由 producer 製作人 preview 試映會 worth 值得的 nominate / nomination 提名 interested 感興趣的 suddenly 突然 title 頭銜（ ）1. items.prompt: Louis：What’s wrong with you, Scott?Scott：What do you mean?Louis：I saw you sleeping in Mrs. Hardacre’s class this morning. If you have any hope of graduating, that is just not done, man.Scott：I’m well aware of that, but I just couldn’t help it. I’m dead tired because I got an hour of sleep at the most last night.Louis：What? Why? All of our big tests are over and done with. That leaves us with more than enough time to take it easy and sleep.Scott：I know, but my lack of sleep has nothing to do with our tests. The apartment across the wall has been rented, so I have a new neighbor and a new problem.Louis：What did he or she do to bother you?Scott：I was bothered by her knocking over and over again on my door last night.Louis：How rude! Did you call the police?Scott：No, because I was busy singing karaoke. And she even left me a note on my door this morning.Louis：Ah, I now understand the reason for her knocking. graduate 畢業 aware 知道的 lack 缺少 rent 租 neighbor 鄰居 knock 敲 rude 無禮的 karaoke 卡拉OK（ ）1. Which note was left on Scott’s door by his new neighbor? (A) “I really don’t want to call the police, so please turn your TV down when you watch late at night.” (B) “Next time, knock louder because I can’t hear anything when my friends and I are singing karaoke.” (C) “Sorry to hear that you failed your test. I know it because the walls are really thin and you and your friends were talking really loudly last night.” fail 不及格 (D) “Your taste in music isn’t too bad. However, could you not sing after ten at night? I need to be at work very early in the morning. Thanks.”（ ）2. Which of the following is correct? (A) Scott’s neighbor was invited to join him. (B) To Scott, singing is more important than sleeping. (C) Louis knew that Scott has problems sleeping at night. (D) The police were called in to stop the fight between Scott and his neighbor.
choices: “I really don’t want to call the police, so please turn your TV down when you watch late at night.”
“Next time, knock louder because I can’t hear anything when my friends and I are singing karaoke.”
“Sorry to hear that you failed your test. I know it because the walls are really thin and you and your friends were talking really loudly last night.” fail 不及格
“Your taste in music isn’t too bad. However, could you not sing after ten at night? I need to be at work very early in the morning. Thanks.”（ ）2. Which of the following is correct?
Scott’s neighbor was invited to join him.
To Scott, singing is more important than sleeping.
Louis knew that Scott has problems sleeping at night.
The police were called in to stop the fight between Scott and his neighbor.
items.explanation: 1. 從最後一個 Scott 的對話可知，Scott 一整晚都在唱卡拉 OK，吵得他的鄰居無法睡覺，所以留言內容應該是請 Scott 不要超過晚上十點後唱歌比較符合文意。2. 由 Scott 唱歌唱了一整晚而不睡覺可推知，他認為唱歌比睡覺重要。

items.prompt: 選出正確的答案並填入空格中：1. The man ＿＿＿＿＿＿ (has lived / was lived) alone since his parents died.2. Though it was snowing, a lot of people still ＿＿＿＿＿＿ (have gone / went) mountain climbing.3. Jeremy didn’t do well today, but I believe he ＿＿＿＿＿＿ (has done / will do) better in the coming game.4. We ＿＿＿＿＿＿ (visit / have visited) the town many times. We took many pictures there.5. My uncle ＿＿＿＿＿＿ (eats / has eaten) lunch at the same restaurant every day.
items.answer: 1. has lived 2. went 3. will do 4. have visited 5. eats
items.explanation: 1. 由「since＋過去式子句」可知，時間是從過去他的父母過世到現在，用現在完成式。2. 前半句時間點是過去式，後半句動作發生的時間與前半句相同，故用過去式。3. 由 the coming game 可知，事件發生在未來，時態用未來式。4. 由後句在當地拍了多張照片，可知是指到目前的經驗，因此用現在完成式。5. 由 every day 可知是指目前的習慣，因此用現在簡單式。

(B) When is it going to begin? (C) How are they going to do that? (D) Is it because of the rising number of bikers?（ ）3. items.prompt: AI has changed the art world. Today, beautiful pictures may be made by computer programs. The process is very fast. A person just gives the computer a “prompt,” and the AI finishes the picture in a few seconds. Making art is now easier than ever. However, people have argued about a big question: Who is the real artist? The human gives the idea, but the computer does all the drawing. Is the artwork really the person’s own work? Because of this, people have two different ideas. Some believe AI is just a powerful tool, like a high-tech paintbrush. Others think of AI as a co-creator, like a smart working partner. Besides, the biggest problem for many traditional artists is legal rights. For years, AI has been studying millions of pictures online. These pictures were made by human artists. When AI creates a new artwork, is it copying parts of those old pictures? Because of this problem, many artists feel angry. To make the art world fair again, clear rules must be set soon. process 過程 prompt 提示詞 argue 爭論 artist 藝術家 human 人類 powerful 強大的 high-tech paintbrush 高科技的畫筆 partner 夥伴 traditional 傳統的 legal 法律的 online 網路上的 copy 抄襲 fair 公平的（ ）1. What is the main idea of the reading? (A) How fast AI programs can make pictures. (B) Showing the art styles of different AI programs. (C) Why people should stop using AI to make artworks. (D) Who owns the art and how we can make the art world fair.（ ）2. What does a “co-creator” do? (A) Come up with ideas and show it tosomeone else. (B) Make art on his or her own. (C) Work together with another person to finish something. (D) Deal with legal problems.（ ）3. According to the reading, what can we know about the future of AI art? according to 根據 (A) The rules are clear now, so people do not worry about it anymore. (B) AI will only learn from free pictures online in the future. (C) Clear rules must be set to make the art world fair again. (D) Traditional artists will lose their jobs because AI is growing too fast.
choices: How fast AI programs can make pictures.
Showing the art styles of different AI programs.
Why people should stop using AI to make artworks.
Who owns the art and how we can make the art world fair.（ ）2. What does a “co-creator” do?
Come up with ideas and show it tosomeone else.
Make art on his or her own.
Work together with another person to finish something.
Deal with legal problems.（ ）3. According to the reading, what can we know about the future of AI art? according to 根據
The rules are clear now, so people do not worry about it anymore.

Clear rules must be set to make the art world fair again.

items.explanation: 1. (A) 僅為第一段的局部細節；(B) 文中未提及 AI 畫風展示；(C) 文中並未呼籲人類停止創作，可知應選 (D)。2. 由第二段的上下文線索 like a smart working partner（就像個聰明的工作夥伴）可推知，co-creator 意指「共同創作者」，應選 (C)。3. 由文章最後一句可知，To make the art world fair again, clear rules must be set soon.（為了讓藝術界再次公平，必須盡快制定明確的規則），故選 (C)。

items.prompt: Online-merge-Offline Marketing (OMO)What Online-merge-Offline, or OMO, marketing is a way for companies to use online and offline tools together. “Online” means things like websites, apps, and social media. “Offline” means stores, events, and face-to-face. OMO connects these two worlds into an easy shopping experience.How For example, a customer may see a product online, read comments on their phone, and then buy it in a real store. Or a person may visit a store first and later buy the same item online. With OMO, the company shares the same information, price, and service in both places. The idea is to make things easy and clear for customers. They don’t feel a break between online and offline. Everything works well together. OMO marketing helps companies understand customers better and give them what they want at the right time and place. Today, many companies use OMO to stay strong and grow.Why OMO marketing is important now for two main reasons. First, people use phones and the Internet every day. They look for products, read comments, and check prices online. At the same time, they still like to touch products, try them, and talk to the workers in stores. If a company only worries about one side, it may lose customers. OMO lets companies follow how people really shop today. Second, competition is very strong now. Customers have many choices, and they can change to other products easily. OMO helps companies give more to their customers. For example, stores can use online information to push products that people may like. They can also send simple messages, special prices, or notices. This makes customers feel known and cared for. When shopping is easy and friendly, people are therefore more likely to come back. Because of these reasons, OMO marketing is not just useful. items.prompt: Do you know what gender stereotypes are? You might not have heard that term before. However, I’m sure you know what they are, ＿1.＿? The reason I know that is because we have all been exposed to those common ideas of how boys and girls should be and act. In fact, we were exposed to them not long after we were born. You know what I’m talking about. Soon after babies are born, they ＿2.＿ differently because of their gender. Boy babies are put in blue blankets, while girl babies are put in pink ones. That’s not surprising to people in this day and age. However, did you know that blue was first a color for girls and pink for boys? In the past, the first color was seen as softer, and the second one was seen as stronger. ＿3.＿ The gender stereotypes don’t stop there. ＿4.＿, they are told and taught different things about their gender. Girls are encouraged to play with dolls, be quiet, and act like little princesses. ＿5.＿, boys are encouraged to play with trucks, be active, and like sports. I don’t know if you believe that’s how boys and girls are, but you should know that those stereotypes aren’t good for either gender. term 專有名詞 expose 暴露 while 然而 encourage 鼓勵 princess 公主 active 活潑的 if 是否（ ）1. (A) don’t you (B) am I not (C) aren’t they (D) do you（ ）2. (A) have been treated (B) were treating (C) treat (D) are treated（ ）3. (A) I think they’re stupid. (B) Now, that’s surprising, isn’t it? (C) They made me so mad. (D) We got that right, didn’t we?（ ）4. (A) If you think they’re interesting (B) When you’ve experienced them (C) As babies grow into kids (D) Before the problem became worse（ ）5. (A) On the other hand (B) At the end of their lives (C) That is to say (D) As you can see
choices: We got that right, didn’t we?（ ）4.
At the end of their lives
items.explanation: 1. 前句為肯定一般動詞，故附加問句用否定助動詞 don’t。2. 前句用現在式 be 動詞 are，且此句句意為在嬰兒們出生不久後，他們就因為他們的性別而「被差別對待」，故用現在式被動語態 are treated。3. 由前句提出跟現行社會不同的認知可知，此句應為「那很令人驚訝，對吧？」。4. 由前句「性別刻板印象不只如此」可知，此句應為「當嬰兒成長為兒童時」。5. 由前後兩句分別描述女孩與男孩被灌輸的觀念可知，此處連接詞應用帶出另一觀點的 on the other hand。

items.prompt: English is often called “a greedy language.” Many people think so because it often “borrows” words from languages all around the world. This never stops. English keeps borrowing more and more. Of course, it never gives these words back, either. They have become part of everyday English and stay in the dictionary. Take the word “ketchup,” for example. Did you know that this common word for tomato sauce most likely comes from the Chinese word kôe-chiap（茄汁）? Another example is “tsunami.” It comes from Japanese. When you use this word, English speakers will know the meaning. You are talking about a giant ocean wave. Besides these words, many other English terms also help us learn about different cultures. For example, the word for the food, “taco,” is from Spanish. It introduces you to Mexican culture. At the same time, in math class, we learn “algebra.” This word was borrowed from the Arabic al-jabr. It connects us to the Middle East. Each borrowed word shows how people from different places meet and share ideas. These words are like small puzzle pieces. They tell the story of a language shared by the whole world. English is truly full of ideas from around the world.＊Spanish 西班牙文 Mexican 墨西哥的 Arabic 阿拉伯文 tomato sauce 番茄醬汁 borrow 借 likely 可能地 giant 巨大的 wave 海浪 term 術語 culture 文化 introduce 介紹 connect 連結 puzzle 拼圖 whole 整個的 truly 真地（ ）1. What can we infer from the reading? infer 推論 (A) All English words come from either Spanish or Chinese. (B) The word “taco” is not from Asia, but “tsunami” is. Asia 亞洲 (C) Another English word for “algebra” is “al-jabr.” (D) English speakers won’t understand you if you use borrowed words.（ ）2. According to the reading, which has a name that was taken from the Middle East? according to 根據 (A) (B) (C) (D) （ ）3. Why does the writer call English “a greedy language”? (A) English has the largest dictionary in the world. (B) It is a very difficult language for people to learn. (C) It takes words from other languages and keeps them. (D) Many English speakers like to go to different countries.（ ）4. What can we learn about borrowed words from the reading? (A) They are usually not found in the dictionary. (B) They help people learn about different cultures. (C) They are only used to talk about food and nature. (D) They have been given back to their original languages. original 原始的
choices: All English words come from either Spanish or Chinese.
The word “taco” is not from Asia, but “tsunami” is. Asia 亞洲
English speakers won’t understand you if you use borrowed words.（ ）2. According to the reading, which has a name that was taken from the Middle East? according to 根據
（ ）3. Why does the writer call English “a greedy language”?
English has the largest dictionary in the world.
It is a very difficult language for people to learn.
It takes words from other languages and keeps them.
Many English speakers like to go to different countries.（ ）4. What can we learn about borrowed words from the reading?
They are usually not found in the dictionary.
They help people learn about different cultures.

They have been given back to their original languages. original 原始的
items.explanation: 1. 根據第二段，tsunami 來自日本（亞洲），而根據第三段，taco 來自西班牙（非亞洲），故選 (B)。2. 第三段提到 algebra 來自阿拉伯文。而 (A) 圖中的數學代數算式為正解，故選 (A)。3. 第一段解釋了為什麼 English 被稱為「貪心的語言」，因為它從世界各地借字，卻從不歸還，可知答案應選 (C)。4. 第三段提到「許多其他英文術語也幫助我們了解不同文化」，可知答案應選 (B)。

items.prompt: Picture it. You have just gotten into a car, and in no time at all, it drives you home. The surprising thing is that the steering wheel doesn’t need to be controlled. Also, the pedals don’t have to be pushed to make the car go or stop, and you don’t have to pay any mind to or see what’s happening on the roads. Is everything in your hometown the same as before? Have you enjoyed your life back home ＿1.＿ you left here? Have you done anything interesting? items.prompt: Tom was a new student at Green Hill School. He was a little scared because everything was new to him. He wanted to make friends quickly so he would not feel lonely. On his first day, Tom noticed many students were wearing blue shoes. He looked down at his brown shoes and felt a little strange. During lunch, Tom sat with a group of students. They talked a lot about their blue shoes. One girl smiled and asked him, “Why don’t you have blue shoes, Tom?” Tom answered, “_____” The girl looked surprised. “But everyone here is wearing blue shoes. That is what all the students do.” Tom listened and saw that almost everyone was wearing blue shoes. Some students who liked other colors even changed their shoes to blue. Tom started to feel lonely because he was different. He wanted to fit in and be part of the group. The next day, Tom went to the shoe shop near the school. He bought a pair of blue shoes. When he put them on, he felt happy. At school, the students smiled at him and talked to him more. Tom thought about his shoes. They were not special, but wearing blue shoes helped him make friends. One day, in class, the teacher told a story about a boy. He wanted to be himself but changed just to be like others. Tom listened carefully. Then he thought about his own story. Tom learned an important lesson. Sometimes people do things just because others do them. This is called conformity. It means following the group to feel liked and safe. But it is also very good to be brave and show who you really are inside. lonely 孤獨的 fit in 適應（ ）1. Which of the following sentences might be what Tom answered? (A) I don’t have blue ones yet. (B) I like to be different from everyone else. (C) I like my brown shoes; they are my favorites. (D) I didn’t know blue shirts were important here.（ ）2. Why does Tom decide to buy a pair of blue shoes? (A) One of his classmates asked him to do it. (B) He wants to be different from his classmates. (C) He wants to make friends with his classmates. (D) Every student has to wear blue shoes in school.（ ）3. Which of the following is another example of “conformity”? (A) A child eats lunch by himself / herself because he / she likes being different. (B) Someone dresses as he / she wants without worrying about what others think. (C) A person does not want to join a club because it goes against his / her interests. club 社團 (D) A student chooses to wear the same backpack as most students to feel like part of the group. backpack 背包
choices: I don’t have blue ones yet.
I like to be different from everyone else.
I like my brown shoes; they are my favorites.
I didn’t know blue shirts were important here.（ ）2. Why does Tom decide to buy a pair of blue shoes?
One of his classmates asked him to do it.
He wants to be different from his classmates.
He wants to make friends with his classmates.
Every student has to wear blue shoes in school.（ ）3. Which of the following is another example of “conformity”?
A child eats lunch by himself / herself because he / she likes being different.
Someone dresses as he / she wants without worrying about what others think.
A person does not want to join a club because it goes against his / her interests. club 社團
A student chooses to wear the same backpack as most students to feel like part of the group. backpack 背包
items.explanation: 1. 由第二段第一句女孩在 Tom 回答後表現得很驚訝，並強調「這裡每個人都穿藍色鞋子，這是所有學生都會做的事」可知，Tom 的回答顯現出他不知道這項不成文的規定，故選 (C)。2. 由第二段倒數第一句跟第二句可知，Tom 因為不同而感到孤單。他想要融入並成為班上的一分子，故選 (C)。3. 文章最後一段定義 conformity 為「做某些事只是因為別人在做（people do things just because others do them）」，目的是為了「感到被喜歡與安全感（feel liked and safe）」，選項中只有 (D)「學生選擇背和多數人一樣的背包以求融入群體」符合追求群體認同的行為。

I was scared of getting close to them at first, but that changed quickly. When I handed them their Christmas dinners, they showed nothing but joy, love, and thanks. items.prompt: Helen：Peter, you’re free now, aren’t you? Peter：Not really, but I can be. What can I do for you?Helen：I need you to send this package to Mr. Anderson at Matrix Systems right away. Peter：It’s that important, isn’t it? Then express mail will be fast enough for you, won’t it?Helen：No way! That takes at least a day or two, and my client can’t wait around that long for it. Peter：Why not? It’s not like he’s a VIP or anything.Helen：In fact, he is, and he’s leaving on a business trip to Berlin（柏林）, Germany, this afternoon. Now, you can see that express mail won’t be fast enough, can’t you?Peter：Yes, loud and clear. Then I think it’s best to call a messenger over to pick it up this morning.Helen：I was thinking the same thing. Also, can you make sure that they rush it over to Matrix Systems before noon?Peter：That shouldn’t be a problem, but I think it’s going to cost more than the regular price.Helen：Money is not an issue at this point. We really can’t lose this client. express 快遞的 client 客戶 VIP 重要人物 messenger 郵遞員 rush 急送 regular 一般的 issue 問題（ ）1. What do we know about Mr. Anderson? (A) He’s already left on his trip. (B) He is from Berlin, Germany. (C) He is a very important client. (D) He will still be at his office after 2 p.m. today.（ ）2. Why does Helen say that Peter’s first idea won’t work? (A) It’s too slow. (B) It’s fast enough. (C) It costs too much. (D) It takes less than a day.（ ）3. How is Peter going to get the package to the client? (A) Send it by express mail. (B) Ask someone to take it over. (C) Have the client pick it up himself. (D) Take it to the client’s office himself.
choices: He’s already left on his trip.
He is a very important client.
He will still be at his office after 2 p.m. today.（ ）2. Why does Helen say that Peter’s first idea won’t work?
It takes less than a day.（ ）3. How is Peter going to get the package to the client?
Ask someone to take it over.
Have the client pick it up himself.
Take it to the client’s office himself.
items.explanation: 1. 由第四個 Helen 回應「Mr. Anderson 的確是 VIP」以及最後一句「我們絶對不能失去這個客戶」可知，Mr. Anderson 是個重要的客戶。2. 原本 Peter 提議用 express mail 寄包裹，但 Helen 說那會花太長時間，可知這個方法「太慢」。3. 由倒數第二個 Peter 回覆可知，他覺得最好請專人送件。

items.prompt: Reporter：Sandra, you were so great in the new movie, Rich Asians. Would you mind sharing more about the movie with the fans?Sandra：＿1.＿ It’s about how two people find love against all the challenges in their lives.Reporter：I noticed that there are mostly Asians in this Hollywood（好萊塢）movie. It’s been the first one in history, ＿2.＿?Sandra：It might be, or at least the most popular one in modern history! I can’t believe how lucky I was to be a part of it!Reporter：Can you tell us what your career was like before this success?Sandra：It has really opened doors to me for sure. I used to only be given interviews for roles that I was nothing like in my life because of the ＿3.＿ in Hollywood.Reporter：Can you give us some examples?Sandra：For example, there was one time I had to play someone who is really good at math even though that’s my least favorite subject at school.Reporter：Because people think Asians must be good at numbers.Sandra：Exactly! When you look at the industry more closely, you will be surprised at how many Asian doctors there are because that’s how we are seen. ＿4.＿, Asians are just like all the other people! There are Asian actresses, fashion designers, lawyers, and more.Reporter：And do you think what has brought the change?Sandra：I believe it’s more than just this one movie. There have been so many movies with stars from all kinds of different cultures, and ＿5.＿. I think the whole society is ready to break stereotypes and make changes!Reporter：Thank you for the time, and good luck! We hope to see you in more good movies in the future!Sandra：Me too. Thank you! Asian 亞洲人 against 克服 challenge 挑戰 modern 現代的 career 職業生涯 success 成功 interview 面試 exactly 完全正確 industry 產業 designer 設計師 culture 文化 whole 整個的 society 社會（ ）1. (A) No, I can’t help but give it up. (B) No, I’m very excited about it. (C) Yes, I was laughed at by those Asians. (D) Yes, the story was quite boring and stupid.（ ）2. (A) is it (B) isn’t it (C) has it (D) hasn’t it（ ）3. (A) it is filled with stereotypes (B) they are laughed at by people (C) they are well liked by the public (D) this is not what Asians are taught to do
choices: No, I can’t help but give it up.
No, I’m very excited about it.
Yes, I was laughed at by those Asians.
Yes, the story was quite boring and stupid.（ ）2.
they are laughed at by people
they are well liked by the public
this is not what Asians are taught to do
items.explanation: 1. 由後句說明這部電影的主旨可知，「Sandra 感到興奮並願意分享」。2. 由前方的 It’s been (= It has been) 可知為現在完成式，附加問句用現在完成式的否定疑問句。3. 由後文可知，訪談主旨為亞洲人在好萊塢的「刻板印象」，包括擅長數學、職業多為醫生等。4. 前文提及人們會驚覺有許多醫生的角色皆為亞洲演員，後文強調亞洲人可以擔任各種職業，故 To be honest 最符合前後文的語氣轉折。5. 由後句「整個社會都準備好打破刻板印象」可知，這些擁有多元文化背景的電影「深受大眾喜愛」。

items.prompt: 填入正確的動詞形式或附加問句： Kelly is a lovely girl, 1. ＿＿＿＿＿＿ she? She has 2. ＿＿＿＿＿＿ the most beautiful girl in our school since her first grade. She has a twin sister（雙胞胎姐姐）, Jenny. Not only Kelly but also Jenny 3. ＿＿＿＿＿＿ tall and thin. Look! Those girls under the tree 4. ＿＿＿＿＿＿ Kelly and Jenny. They both look beautiful, 5. ＿＿＿＿＿＿ they?

items.prompt: Ann is a big fan of the TV show, “Dark School.” But she fell behind because of her math homework. The latest episode just came out. Ann knows the Internet is now full of spoilers, but she decided to check social media anyway. Ann saw a post about the final boss. Her friend, Clara, called right away. Clara is good at using computers. “We must start the Mute Plan,” Clara said. “It will protect you from spoilers!” Ann opened her phone settings and made a “Spoiler Blacklist.” She added the show’s name, the main characters’ names, and some words like “big fire,” “married,” and “dream.” Clara also told her to add “singing rabbit,” just in case. After the settings changed, Ann’s social media page looked empty. Only boring pictures of her aunt’s cookies were left. Just then, her brother Jay, the human “Spoiler Machine,” ran into her room. “Ann! The bad guy…” Ann acted quickly. She didn’t cover her ears. She put her phone screen on Jay’s mouth to stop him from talking. Anyone who spoils the story must be stopped! Clara spoke through the phone, “Great job, Ann! Your defense system is perfect!” Ann laughed. The phone on the table gave her peace. She was ready for a weekend without spoilers. episode 劇集 spoiler 劇透 social media 社群媒體 mute 靜音 setting 設定 character 角色 in case 以防萬一 empty 空的 human 人類 defense system 防禦系統（ ）1. How does the writer tell this story? (A) The writer compares the good parts and bad parts of using social media. (B) The writer describes a problem Ann faced and the smart way she fixed it. (C) The writer lists four different ideas that Ann and Clara had for the weekend. (D) The writer explains some rules and tells people how to talk to their brother or sister.（ ）2. What did Ann do to protect herself from spoilers on social media? (A) She decided not to surf the Internet. (B) She asked Clara to watch the show for her. (C) She turned off her phone for the weekend. (D) She made a “Spoiler Blacklist” on her phone.（ ）3. What does the word “Spoiler Machine” probably mean? (A) A robot that can clean itself. (B) An exciting computer game. (C) A person who tells the story too early. (D) A machine which is used to break cookies.（ ）4. Which is true? (A) Ann stopped her brother before he could spoil the story. (B) Jay is Ann’s math teacher, and he often gives lots of homework. (C) Ann blocked all posts from Clara, and they don’t talk to each other now. (D) Ann was busy with her homework, but she still made time for her favorite TV show.（ ）5. What is the correct order of what happened in the story? (A) 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 (B) 4 → 3 → 1 → 2 (C) 2 → 4 → 1 → 3 (D) 3 → 4 → 2 → 1
choices: The writer compares the good parts and bad parts of using social media.
The writer describes a problem Ann faced and the smart way she fixed it.
The writer lists four different ideas that Ann and Clara had for the weekend.
The writer explains some rules and tells people how to talk to their brother or sister.（ ）2. What did Ann do to protect herself from spoilers on social media?
She decided not to surf the Internet.
She asked Clara to watch the show for her.
She turned off her phone for the weekend.
She made a “Spoiler Blacklist” on her phone.（ ）3. What does the word “Spoiler Machine” probably mean?
A robot that can clean itself.
A person who tells the story too early.
A machine which is used to break cookies.（ ）4. Which is true?
Ann stopped her brother before he could spoil the story.
Jay is Ann’s math teacher, and he often gives lots of homework.
Ann blocked all posts from Clara, and they don’t talk to each other now.
Ann was busy with her homework, but she still made time for her favorite TV show.（ ）5. What is the correct order of what happened in the story?
items.explanation: 1. 本文描述了問題（Ann 擔心被劇透） → 解決方案（Clara 教她使用 Mute Plan） → 結果（Ann 成功避開劇透），故應選 (B)。2. 由第三段第一句「Ann 打開手機設置，創建了一個『劇透黑名單』。」可知，答案應選 (D)。3. 文中 Jay 被叫做 the human “Spoiler Machine” 並且準備要跟 Ann 說劇情內容，可推知意思是會劇透的人，故選 (C)。4. 選項 (B) Jay 並非 Ann的數學老師，而是她弟弟，故錯誤；選項 (C) Ann 封鎖的是社群媒體上有關劇情的關鍵字，並非 Clara 的貼文，故錯誤；選項 (D) Ann 之前忙於數學作業，沒有辦法看最喜歡的劇集，故錯誤。5. 四個事件的順序依序為：「《黑暗學校》新一集上線。」→「Ann 在社群媒體上看到劇透。」→「Clara 打電話給 Ann，給她一個計畫。」→「Clara 為 Ann 的快速反應歡呼。」，故應選 (B)。

items.prompt: All people like a good story, ＿1.＿? Well, here’s one for you all to think about. There was once a young wild deer. He lived in the middle of a beautiful thick forest. He spent almost all of his time ＿2.＿ fresh green plants because he loved their taste. Sounds wonderful, doesn’t it? One day, he found some new green leaves on a tree and started eating them happily. Then he heard a noise, so he stopped and looked around. He saw some hunters, and they were looking right at him. The deer tried to run away, but the hunters ran after him. That was scary, ＿3.＿? Lucky for the deer, he saw some grapevines, so he quickly went behind them. The hunters couldn’t find him. They thought that he was long gone, so they stopped and went back. The deer believed that they left, so he began to relax. ＿4.＿ Then he caught the smell of the grape leaves. He thought they would taste delicious, so he started to eat them. However, that was a big mistake because the hunters heard the noise. They shot into the grapevines, and the deer fell. He knew then that it was a bad idea to eat the leaves, but it was too late. wild 野生的 deer 鹿 plant 植物 leaves 葉子 hunter 獵人 grapevine 葡萄藤 relax 放鬆 shoot / shot 射擊（ ）1. (A) does he (B) don’t they (C) do you (D) didn’t we（ ）2. (A) will eat (B) to eat (C) was eating (D) eating（ ）3. (A) didn’t it (B) didn’t that (C) wasn’t this (D) wasn’t it（ ）4. (A) Well, who wouldn’t? (B) It isn’t right to go there, is it? (C) He knew that they would come back. (D) The hunters were happy to see him do that.
choices: It isn’t right to go there, is it?
He knew that they would come back.
The hunters were happy to see him do that.
items.explanation: 1. 由 All people 及 like 可知，附加問句用 don’t they。2. spend 後方應接動名詞（V-ing）。3. 由 That was 可知，附加問句用 wasn’t it。4. 由前句「鹿以為獵人已經走了，所以他開始放鬆」及後面描述他吃葡萄葉可知，此句應為「嗯，誰不會呢？」。

items.prompt: Dear Dr. Frank Smith,I’m writing about the vet technician job at your animal hospital. I wish you were still looking for one. Also, I did a lot of them without the vet’s help. Over the years, I have not only treated the animals but also helped their owners. For them, taking their pets to the vet can be a hard time, so I do everything possible to make them feel at ease. The animals mean everything to them, don’t they? At the moment, I’m working for a young vet at a small clinic. Although he knows I can do the simple procedures without any problems, he chooses to do everything himself. Therefore, I haven’t used my skills for some time now. I can’t continue like this, so I would like the chance to meet and discuss my coming to work for you.Sincerely,Abby Normal vet technician 獸醫技術員 posting 網站上公布的資訊 simple 簡易的 procedure 手術；醫療處理 at ease 安心 clinic 診所 therefore 因此 skill 技術 continue 繼續 discuss 討論（ ）1. Why did Abby email Dr. Smith? (A) To ask about work. (B) To find out about her health. (C) To get him to look at her pet. (D) To ask him about her vet boyfriend.（ ）2. Which of the following is true? (A) Dr. Smith has already found someone. (B) Abby cares about people and animals. (C) Abby hasn’t worked on cats or dogs by herself. (D) Dr. Smith won’t let Abby treat any pets at his clinic.（ ）3. If you continue to treat pet owners badly, we’re going to have to let you go.

items.prompt: Although she is already one of the most successful stars in the world, you’ve probably never heard of the singer’s real name, Stefani Germanotta. That’s because almost everyone knows her by the name of Lady Gaga. She got the name from the 1984 Queen song Radio Ga Ga. However, Lady Gaga was not always popular and successful. In fact, she faced rejection and bullying in her young life. When she was a student in New York University (NYU), there was a Facebook group called “Stefani Germanotta, you’ll never be famous.” Things like that didn’t stop her, and she never gave up her dream. Finally, her hard work paid off when her first record, The Fame, hit the US stores on August 19, 2008. In 2019, she became the FIRST woman in history to win an Oscar, Grammy, BAFTA, and Golden Globe all in the same year－all for the movie, A Star is Born. Now she is famous and has fans all over the world. “There can be 100 people in a room, and 99 don’t believe in you. And you just need 1 person to believe in you,” she said the same thing again and again. items.prompt: Palm reading can give you some ideas about yourself. Before you try it, you need to know what the most important lines are and where they are on your palm. First is the big line that begins at the side of the palm between the thumb and index finger and usually goes down to the wrist. It is called the life line, and it gives you an idea about your health and how long you may live. Next is the line that starts at the same place as the life line and goes across the palm. It is called the head line, and its length tells how smart you may be. The longer it is, the smarter you are. Above that is the heart line. It runs across the palm to below the little finger at the edge of the hand. It shows how strong your heart is and how you feel about love. The last line runs from the bottom of the palm up to the bottom of the middle finger. It is called the fate line. It shows when and how you may become successful in life. palm 手掌 thumb 拇指 index finger 食指 wrist 手腕 edge 邊緣 fate 命運（ ）1. Which line is line ②? (A) The heart line. (B) The head line. (C) The fate line. (D) The life line.（ ）2. What does “its length” mean? (A) How big the palm is. (B) How long the head line is. (C) How strong the heart line is. (D) How short the middle finger is.（ ）3. Which is correct? (A) The heart line tells a person’s feelings. feelings 感覺 (B) The life line is all about a person’s money. (C) The fate line shows how smart a person is. (D) The head line tells when a person’s life ends.
choices: The life line.（ ）2. What does “its length” mean?
How long the head line is.
How strong the heart line is.
How short the middle finger is.（ ）3. Which is correct?
The heart line tells a person’s feelings. feelings 感覺
The life line is all about a person’s money.
The fate line shows how smart a person is.
The head line tells when a person’s life ends.
items.explanation: 1. 第四段提到，從手腕底部到中指下方的這條線，稱為「命運線」。2. 第三段提到，智慧線（the head line）越長的人，越聰明。故 its length 表智慧線「長度」之意。3. 第三段最後一句提到，感情線（the heart line）顯示你心臟的強度以及你對愛的感覺。

It’s not sweet, but a little salty. ＿3.＿ Besides, many TV shows have reported on it. James：Sounds cool, but I don’t believe food shows. I ＿4.＿ some snacks at the night markets because of their recommendation. However, most of them tasted terrible. pudding 布丁 salty 鹹的 recommendation 推薦（ ）1. (A) Do you feel hungry? items.prompt: In 2002, Teun van de Keuken, a Dutch reporter, found out that all the chocolate companies that agreed to Harkin–Engel Protocol didn’t follow the rules of making slave-free chocolate. So, he decided to take action himself. Instead of writing news about the case, he recorded himself eating illegally-made chocolate and sent the video to the court. Though this case made more people care about how the chocolate ＿1.＿ they bought was made, most big chocolate companies still showed little interest in producing chocolate differently. In November 2005, he made milk chocolate that used 100% slave-free cocoa under his own company, Tony’s Chocolonely. The name of the company comes from the fact that he created the business all by himself without any help from the chocolate industry. The chocolate ＿2.＿ package was in bright red color caught everyone’s eye successfully. Since then, the company has produced and sold chocolate closely following the rules of fair trade. They pay farmers 25% more than the market price for their cocoa, so they can keep their profits as big as possible. It’s clear that a lot of work still needs to be done. ＿3.＿, Tony’s Chocolonely created “Tony’s in Africa” project in 2009 to try even harder to change the cocoa industry. They’ve given 1% of their profits to the project every year and hope that the dream of 100% slave-free chocolate around the world ＿4.＿. By buying their chocolate, we can also help change the world. Dutch 荷蘭的 protocol 議定書 slave 奴隸 illegally 違法地 court 法院 cocoa 可可粉 industry 工業 fair trade 公平貿易 profit 利潤 project 計畫（ ）1. (A) whose (B) who (C) what (D) ╳（ ）2. (A) which (B) that (C) whose (D) ╳（ ）3. (A) However (B) Therefore (C) In a word (D) On the other hand（ ）4. (A) will become a leader (B) will be dealt with in the future (C) is doing something simple (D) can be fulfilled one day
choices: will be dealt with in the future
items.explanation: 1. 先行詞 the chocolate 是物，關係代名詞要用 which 或 that，此處關係代名詞在關係子句中為受詞，故可省略。2. 空格後為名詞 package，隸屬於先行詞 chocolate，故用關係代名詞 whose 代替所有格。3. 由前句「仍然有很多工作需要做」及後句提到 “Tony’s in Africa” project 可知，此處用 therefore 表「因此」才符合語意。4. 由前文 Tony’s Chocolonely 每年提供計畫 1% 的利潤可知，此句是希望 100% 無奴隸巧克力的夢想「有天能被實踐」才符合語意。

items.prompt: Have you ever heard of the “Decoy Effect”? It is a common pricing strategy. Sometimes, a company gives you two choices: Option A is cheap but basic, and Option B is expensive but very good. When you don’t know which one to choose, the company adds a third choice: Decoy C. Decoy C costs almost the same as Option B, but it is not as good. The companies don’t really want to sell Decoy C. They just want you to think, “If I pay a little more money, I can get Option B!” This makes you feel Option B is a great deal, so you decide to buy the expensive plan. Let’s look at an example. It is July now. Tom and his older brother are on their summer vacation. They play video games on their phones from 9:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. every night. They want to buy new phone plans. Tom looks at two companies: Happy Mobile and Best Mobile. Happy MobileSpecial Offers1. Two Friends Offer Do you want Plan B (10 GB)? Buy it with a friend! You and your friend only pay $400 each. 2. Winter Surprise Buy any plan in January or February. We give you 5 GB free Internet!Best MobileSpecial Offers1. Family Offer Buy Plan 3 for $1198. Your mom, dad, or brother buys the same plan, and they only pay $599. 2. Summer Nights Offer In July and August, the Internet is free from 8:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. every night! effect 效應 pricing strategy 定價策略 option 選項 basic 基礎的 mobile 電信 unlimited 無限的 offer 優惠方案（ ）1. What does “They” mean in the reading? (A) Tom and his brother. (B) Two friends. (C) The companies (D) People who buy Decoy C.（ ）2. What does a “decoy” do in a pricing strategy? (A) It leads to spending more money. (B) It gives you a half price discount. (C) It helps people save a lot of money. (D) It tells you to buy the cheapest plan.（ ）3. Tom and his brother want to spend the least money. They only need Internet for their video games from 9:30 p.m. to 10:30 p.m. every night. Which plan is the best choice for them? (A) Best Mobile - Plan 2. (B) Happy Mobile - Plan A. (C) Best Mobile - Plan 3 (with Family Offer). (D) Best Mobile - Plan 1 (with Summer Nights Offer).
choices: People who buy Decoy C.（ ）2. What does a “decoy” do in a pricing strategy?
It leads to spending more money.
It gives you a half price discount.
It helps people save a lot of money.

It tells you to buy the cheapest plan.（ ）3. Tom and his brother want to spend the least money. They only need Internet for their video games from 9:30 p.m. to 10:30 p.m. every night. Which plan is the best choice for them?
items.explanation: 1. 由前一句 The companies don’t really want to sell Decoy C. 可知，They 指的就是前一句的主詞 The companies（企業），故選 (C)。2. 第二段最後一句可知，誘餌 (decoy) 讓人最終購買最貴的方案，故應選 (A)。3. 根據文章第四段第一句可知現在是七月，又 Tom 和哥哥玩手機遊戲的時間落在免費時段，所以他們不需要買大流量的方案，故 Best Mobile 的 Plan 1 搭配 Summer Nights Offer 的方案是所有選項中最便宜的，故選 (D)。

What does “they” refer to? refer to 意指 (A) The ways of living. (B) People who love shopping. (C) Things that are poorly made. (D) The president of Uruguay and the writer.（ ）2. According to the letter, who has found real happiness? according to 根據 (A) Mike. He cares about his family and friends. (B) Cindy. She doesn’t talk to anyone around her. (C) Jack. He works fourteen hours a day to pay for his car. (D) Mary. She shouts at her parents every time she feels angry.（ ）3. What do we learn from the reading? items.prompt: Ethan：Mrs. Lo, what’s the matter with Sean? ＿1.＿Mrs. Lo：I have no idea. Aren’t you guys in the band together? How come you don’t know what’s wrong?Ethan：I was in the restroom, so I don’t know what happened.Mrs. Lo：I see. Let’s ask Sean and check out what happened to him.(Mrs. Lo and Ethan go up to Sean.)Mrs. Lo：Sean, what’s wrong? Why are you crying?Sean：I’m not doing well in the band because I don’t know ＿2.＿ to play the new song.Mrs. Lo：Don’t worry so much. You just need to practice more. Besides, you can always ask your friends to help you ＿3.＿ you have any problems.Ethan：That’s right. You can come to me anytime. That’s what friends are for, ＿4.＿?Sean：Thank you, Mrs. Lo. And it’s so kind of you to say that, Ethan. band 樂團（ ）1. (A) Do you know why he is crying? (B) Why don’t you help me find out? (C) Let’s check out what’s happening. (D) I should put myself in his shoes.（ ）2. (A) what (B) where (C) how (D) why（ ）3. (A) if (B) what (C) though (D) so（ ）4. (A) aren’t they (B) is it (C) are they (D) isn’t it
choices: Do you know why he is crying?
Why don’t you help me find out?
I should put myself in his shoes.（ ）2.

Luckily, there is also “JOMO,” or the “joy of missing out.” It tells us a different idea: being alone and taking time out from the Internet is a good thing. You may be surprised to find other sources for new English words. Where does the noun “stan” come from? The answer can be found in pop culture. “Stans” are crazy fans. They love famous people so much that they often do extreme things to follow their favorite stars. This term was first heard in a song by Eminem in 2000. This song is called “Stan.” It tells a story about a crazy music fan. items.prompt: The Human LibraryWhat is the Human Library? This project started at a music festival with a simple but strong goal: to create a safe space to talk and change stereotypes. For example, when people see a man with many tattoos, they may think he is scary or dangerous. However, he may actually be very kind. That brings us to our main goal and most important rule:*“Don’t judge a book by its cover.”How Does a “Reading” Work? A “reading” is a 30-minute talk. In the first 5 minutes, the “book” tells you about himself or herself. Then, you can ask questions. ①One-on-one reading: one person reads one book at one event.②Group reading: 4 to 6 people sit together to read one book for half an hour. They can read up to three books during one event.What are the Rules? Just like a real library, readers must respect the “books.” Below are the four rules you should follow: ①Give the book back on time. This sets a clear end time for the talk. It protects the “books” and makes sure they don’t get too tired.②Don’t break the pages. This means readers should be friendly and nice. They shouldn’t ask questions that will hurt the person.③Don’t write on the book. This tells readers not to push their own stereotypes onto the “books.” They should just listen and try to understand.④Don’t take the book home. This draws a clear line between people who meet at the event. Readers and “books” shouldn’t bother each other after the event. What’s a “Book Depot”? The “books” rest in a room before they meet their readers. During this time, they talk to each other. Although they are very different from one another, they often become good friends there. ＊Human Library 真人圖書館 project 計畫 goal 目標 stereotype 刻板印象 tattoo 刺青 one-on-one 一對一 event 活動 respect 尊重 book depot 書庫（ ）1. What does “judge a book by its cover” mean? (A) To write down new ideas while listening. (B) To decide what a person or a thing is like. (C) To read a book carefully from cover to cover. (D) To make friends with someone who is different.（ ）2. What is the reading mainly about? (A) A music festival with famous singers. (B) A special library with many old paper books. (C) A project for people to share their life stories. (D) A place that lets people talk when reading books.（ ）3. Which is true about the Human Library? (A) You can take your favorite “book” home after reading. (B) The “book” will ask you questions for the first 5 minutes. (C) The “books” in the waiting room never talk to each other. (D) You can read a “book” with your friends at the same time.
choices: To write down new ideas while listening.
To decide what a person or a thing is like.
To read a book carefully from cover to cover.
To make friends with someone who is different.（ ）2. What is the reading mainly about?

(A) 音樂祭只是起源背景，並非本文主題；(B) 真人圖書館是與「真人」對話；(C) 全文主旨在介紹「真人圖書館」透過對話分享人生故事、打破刻板印象的計畫，故 (C) 正確；(D) 本文介紹的是透過與「真人圖書」對話的活動，而非閱讀紙本書籍的場所。3. (A) 根據規則四，禁止把書帶回家；(B) 談話的前五分鐘，應為「真人圖書」自我介紹；(C) 文末 Book Depot 段落提及，真人圖書在書庫等待時會聊天並成為好友；(D) 根據 How Does a “Reading” Work? 的第二點「團體借閱」，可知能夠與朋友同時閱覽，故 (D) 正確。

items.prompt: Many people have noticed the special language of Gen Z. These young people, born between 1997 and 2012, have grown up online. Because of the Internet, their communication happens very quickly. To them, traditional English sometimes feels too slow. Therefore, they have created many new words to fully express their ideas. For example, the word “slay” once meant “to kill.” Now, it means “to do something well” or “to look amazing.” This change reflects the fast development of language today. Gen Z mainly uses two ways to make these new words. The first way is using abbreviations to help them type faster. For example, “GOAT” stands for the “Greatest Of All Time.” The second way is combining two words to describe new ideas. “Vibe check” means to see someone’s mood. These special words are used by these young people to understand each other in a short time. Although these words work online, they are often seen as inappropriate for school reports or job interviews. In those cases, formal language is needed. items.prompt: People have great ideas for their own shops and companies. However, they don’t always have the funds to get them off the ground, do they? They have several ways of getting the money. The old way is to go to a bank, apply for a loan, and hope they get it. That takes time, doesn’t it? Also, people don’t know if they will get the loan because it depends on what a small group of people think of their ideas. Now, there’s a new way to get things started. It is an international money collecting website called Indiegogo. The company is in San Francisco and was started by Eric Schell, Slava Rubin, and Danae Ringelmann in 2008. Indiegogo helps people get their interesting ideas out there. It also gives them control over their own projects. Basically, people with the ideas make a webpage for their projects, and on it, they tell others what they are doing and what kind of help they need. The more people see their pages and donate, the more money they will raise. If none is raised, they don’t need to pay Indiegogo. For those that have raised enough money to start their projects, a small fee is required for using Indiegogo’s website. It’s a win-win for both sides, isn’t it? get sth off the ground 使……開始 apply for a loan 申請貸款 if 是否 depend on 取決於 international 國際的 website 網站 control 控制 project 企劃 basically 基本上 webpage 網頁 donate 捐錢 none 沒有東西 fee 費用 require 需要（ ）1. (C) They are the old way for people to donate. (D) People never get enough money from them.（ ）3. What do people on Indiegogo have to do? (A) Tell banks all their money problems. (B) Pay a fee if they raise enough money. (C) Take care of other people’s webpages. (D) Ask the website to talk about their projects.（ ）4. What can we learn about Indiegogo? (A) Three bank workers started it. (B) It has offices all over the USA. (C) It is only for people with money. (D) People all over the world can use it.

items.prompt: Young people can create great things when they face a problem and try to fix it. Many young inventors saw problems in everyday life and created simple, helpful ideas. Here are four examples that show how kids can change the world.Gabby Bows Gabby Goodwin was only seven when she had a big problem: Her hair clips always fell out. She lost them at school, at home, and even on the playground. To solve this, she invented Gabby Bows, a hair clip with a special double-snap design. It holds hair well and stays on all day. Gabby Bows make hair look cute and help kids stop losing clips.Makin’ Bacon Makin’ Bacon is a special plate for the microwave. Abbey Fleck was just eight when she invented it. Her family wanted to cook bacon but did not want too much oil. So Abbey made Makin’ Bacon. The bacon hangs on a bar when it cooks, so the extra oil runs down. It is easy to use, and the bacon is cooked in a healthier way.Summly When Nick D’Aloisio was fifteen, he felt tired of reading long news stories. He wanted quick information for school, so he built Summly, an app that reads many reports and shows short summaries. Users open the app, choose a topic, and see the key points in seconds. Summly helps people save time and learn faster.Nohbo Soap At sixteen, Benjamin Stern worried about plastic trash from shampoo bottles. To protect the Earth, he invented Nohbo soap, a small soap drop used only once. It melts in water and needs no plastic at all. It is convenient to carry and friendly to nature. These young people showed that age doesn’t matter. If you see a problem, maybe you can invent something amazing, too. inventor / invent 發明家╱發明 solve 解決 clip 夾子 double 兩次 snap 按 bacon 培根 microwave 微波爐 extra 額外的 summary 摘要 shampoo 洗髮精 melt 融化（ ）1. What is the reading mainly about? (A) How to cook better food. (B) The history of hair clips and hair soap. (C) Why kids do not like to read long stories. (D) Young people who fix problems by creating things.（ ）2. What does Abbey Fleck’s invention look like? (A) (B) (C) (D) （ ）3. Sally wants to quickly find out what is happening around the world. Which invention should she use? (A) Nick’s invention. (B) Abbey’s invention. (C) Gabby’s invention. (D) Benjamin’s invention.
choices: The history of hair clips and hair soap.
Why kids do not like to read long stories.
Young people who fix problems by creating things.（ ）2. What does Abbey Fleck’s invention look like?
（ ）3. Sally wants to quickly find out what is happening around the world. Which invention should she use?
items.explanation: 1. 文章開頭和結尾都強調「年輕人看到問題並創造東西來解決」，故主要內容是關於透過創造來解決問題的年輕人，可知應選 (D)。2. 根據文章內容，Abbey Fleck 發明了 Makin’ Bacon，那是一種可用於微波爐的培根烹煮器具，故相近的圖片應選 (C)。3. Sally 想要快速了解世界各地正在發生的事情，所以應該要使用 Summly，也就是 Nick D’Aloisio 的發明，故應選 (A)。

items.prompt: Kara：Hey, Tim. Do you have any idea ＿1.＿ my mask is? I’ve looked for it everywhere, but I still can’t find it.Tim：I don’t know ＿2.＿. You’re not sick or anything. Besides, it’s too hot to wear one out today.Kara：I know. It’s just that the air quality is so bad that I don’t want to leave the house ＿3.＿.Tim：Really? How can you tell it’s that bad?Kara：The weather report said ＿4.＿ on a scale from 1 to 10, with 10 being the worst, we’re at a 10 today.Tim：Man, that is dangerous. We’re usually at a 3 at this time of year.Kara：The report also said the poor air quality is brought by a cold front coming from the northwest. Tim：No way! I thought all the big dark clouds in the sky were a sign of a storm coming our way.Kara：＿5.＿ Tim：I see. Then I think I should get myself a mask, too. too… to 太……而不能 quality 品質 so… that 如此……以致於 scale 等級 cold front 冷鋒 storm 暴風雨（ ）1. (A) what (B) how (C) where (D) if（ ）2. (A) why you would need that (B) how you found that (C) if you will give me one, too (D) where you bought it（ ）3. (A) in such hot weather (B) without putting one on first (C) if it keeps raining (D) after it gets dark（ ）4. (A) if (B) what (C) when (D) that（ ）5. (A) Thanks for telling me about that. (B) Why didn’t I think of that? (C) That’s not the case at all. (D) Maybe what you thought was also right.
choices: if you will give me one, too
Thanks for telling me about that.
Why didn’t I think of that?
That’s not the case at all.
Maybe what you thought was also right.
items.explanation: 1. 由下句到處在找口罩可知，此句應為「你知道我的口罩在哪裡嗎？」，故疑問詞用 where。2. 由下句「你沒有生病或怎麼了」可知，此句應為「我不知道你為何需要口罩」。3. 根據上下文意，此句應為「只是空氣品質太糟，以致於我不想沒先戴上口罩就出門」才符合語意。4. 根據此句語意可知，空格內應填入 that，以引導名詞子句作為動詞 said 的受詞。5. 根據上下文意，此句應為「事實不是那樣」才符合語意。

items.prompt: On a high mountain in the east of the country, something interesting happened. A new lake appeared. It was a surprise for everyone. But how did this lake come to be? It all started with an earthquake. The ground began to shake. Many large rocks and mud slid down from the top of the mountain into a river below. The rocks and mud made a huge wall and blocked the river. The river water could not flow forward. Day by day, the water behind this new wall got higher and higher. Soon, a new lake was born. The lake was very large and deep. It held a large amount of water, almost like a small sea. People who lived in the town near the mountain were very worried. They were afraid that the wall of rocks and mud was not strong enough. “What if the wall breaks?” they asked. It was a very serious problem. They knew it could be very dangerous if the water broke through the wall. Then, a typhoon came. It was a terrible storm with strong winds and heavy rain. The rain fell for many days. A large amount of water flowed into the new lake. The lake became very full. The water level rose higher and higher. Finally, the water started to flow over the wall. At first, it was a small stream, but soon it became a powerful river. The water rushed down the mountain with a loud sound. It was a scary sight. The river flowed quickly towards the town downstream, carrying rocks, mud, and debris. Houses near the riverbank were flooded, and some roads were washed away. People had to move to safer places. The town faced great damage, but the early warnings helped save many lives. This event showed everyone the power of nature. We must always be careful and respect the world around us. appear 出現 mud 泥巴 huge 巨大的 flow 流動 forward 向前 amount 數量 storm 暴風雨 stream 溪流 rush 衝 downstream 下游 damage 損害 warning 警告 event 事件 respect 尊敬（ ）1. What does “debris” most likely mean? most likely 最有可能 (A) Plants growing near the lake. plant 植物 (B) Clean water flowing down the river. (C) Broken rocks, mud, and pieces carried by the floodwater. (D) People moving to safer places in the town.（ ）2. Please read the four events below and choose the correct order:a. A typhoon brought heavy rain, causing the water level in the new lake to rise quickly.b. An earthquake happened, causing rocks and mud to slide down and block a river.c. The water broke through the wall, running down the mountain and flooding the town.d. Water gathered behind the blockage, slowly forming a large new lake. gather 聚集 blockage 阻塞物 (A) a → c → b → d (B) b → d → a → c (C) d → a → c → b (D) b → a → d → c
choices: Plants growing near the lake. plant 植物
Clean water flowing down the river.
Broken rocks, mud, and pieces carried by the floodwater.

People moving to safer places in the town.（ ）2. Please read the four events below and choose the correct order:a. A typhoon brought heavy rain, causing the water level in the new lake to rise quickly.b. An earthquake happened, causing rocks and mud to slide down and block a river.c. The water broke through the wall, running down the mountain and flooding the town.d. Water gathered behind the blockage, slowly forming a large new lake. gather 聚集 blockage 阻塞物
items.explanation: 1. 文中提到河流快速流向城鎮時，帶著「rocks（岩石）, mud（泥土）and debris」。這暗示 debris 是一種與岩石、泥土類似，且會被洪水沖刷下來的物質，故選 (C)。2. 根據文章敘述，事件發生的先後順序如下：事件 b：首先發生了地震（earthquake），導致岩石與泥土滑落並阻塞河流。事件 d：河水在阻塞物（blockage）後方聚集，慢慢形成了一個新湖泊（a new lake was born）。事件 a：隨後颱風（typhoon）來襲，強降雨導致湖泊水位（water level）快速上升。事件 c：最後水流衝破土石牆，奔向山下並淹沒了城鎮（flooded the town）。正確的發展順序為 b → d → a → c，故選 (B)。

items.prompt: Dear Ms. Chou,I am the principal of the school that your son goes to. You may not remember me, but we met at the Parent-Teacher Day last year. I’m writing to you today because I have some news about Jay that you may not be happy to hear.In the past few weeks, several of Jay’s teachers have come to me. All of them said that he didn’t behave, either in or out of class. He didn’t care even after he was given warnings and told to stop. His actions have led to problems in classes, and some of his classmates were hurt by the things he said and did. The teachers also told me that they’ve written to you many times about this, but you haven’t answered yet.I think the best way to fix this problem is for you to come and have a talk with me. With your help, we might have a better chance of understanding what’s going on with Jay. If I fail to hear from you, stronger action may be taken to stop him from acting this way.Sincerely,Randall Kelly principal 校長 behave 行為檢點 warning 警告（ ）1. What is the purpose of this e-mail? purpose 目的 (A) To fool a student and his parent. (B) To get a student’s parent to do something. (C) To tell a student’s parent about an annual meeting. annual 一年一次的 (D) To report a problem to teachers.（ ）2. What did Jay NOT do? (A) Hurt other students. (B) Care little about warnings. (C) Listen to his teachers. (D) Do bad things at school.
choices: To fool a student and his parent.
To get a student’s parent to do something.
To tell a student’s parent about an annual meeting. annual 一年一次的
To report a problem to teachers.（ ）2. What did Jay NOT do?

items.prompt: A Successful Mistake - Post-it Notes How does a mistake become a successful product? Post-it Notes are a good example. In 1968, a 3M researcher, Spencer Silver, was trying to make a very strong glue to be used in building planes. However, he came up with something different instead. He made a very weak glue. At the time, nobody could think of a use for this weak glue, but he believed he would find a use for it one day. Many years later, another 3M researcher, Arthur Fry, had a problem of losing his notes in his church song book. He was tired of that. One day, an idea came into Arthur’s mind. He remembered Spencer’s glue and tried some on his bookmarks. It worked wonderfully! Arthur saw that his bookmarks stayed in place. To his surprise, he could easily take them away from the pages and stick them again. In 1974, the idea of Post-it Note was born, and Arthur then started making the notes with Silver’s glue for 3M. Spencer, Arthur, and their team spent several years working to make sure the glue stayed on the piece of note but not on the page. After a successful product test, Post-it Notes hit the market in 1980. Since then, Post-it Notes have become one of the most popular office products in the world. There are now more than 600 Post-it Note products sold in more than 100 countries. Have you ever used Post-it Notes? What do you think of this successful mistake? Post-it Note 便利貼 product 產品 researcher 研究員 glue 膠；膠水 weak 不合標準的 bookmark 書籤 stick 黏貼 born 誕生的（ ）1. What is the topic of this reading? (A) Tips for writing notes. (B) The history of Post-it Notes. (C) A successful company－3M. (D) Ways to stop making mistakes.（ ）2. What does “that” refer to? refer to 意指 (A) Arthur couldn’t find his church song book. (B) Spencer couldn’t stop making mistakes on his job. (C) Arthur was bored with his job as a researcher. (D) Arthur’s notes kept falling out of his church song book. （ ）3. What is the correct order of the following events? ① 3M held a market test and began selling Post-it Notes. ② Spencer made weak glue, and nobody was interested in it. ③ Arthur put glue on a piece of paper and used the paper as a bookmark. ④ Researchers tried to find a way to get the glue to stick to the note and not come off. (A) ①④②③ (B) ④②③① (C) ②③④① (D) ②③①④
choices: Ways to stop making mistakes.（ ）2. What does “that” refer to? refer to 意指
Arthur couldn’t find his church song book.
Spencer couldn’t stop making mistakes on his job.
Arthur was bored with his job as a researcher.

Arthur’s notes kept falling out of his church song book. （ ）3. items.explanation: 1. 由標題與文章中重複出現 Post-it Notes，而文章依時序說明便利貼的發想、產出到銷售，可知主題與便利貼的歷史有關。2. 前句提到他歌本上的便條紙常會不見，故對此感到厭煩，並且想找到解決此問題的辦法。3. 由時間排序的關鍵字可知以下事件排序：首先，Spencer 在 1968 年製造出一種黏性弱的膠水。多年後，Arthur 利用 Spencer 的膠水在書籤上。接著，兩人的團隊進行測試與改良 ，確保膠水附著在便利貼上，而不是書本的頁面。最後終於成功通過商品測試，並在 1980 年上市販售。故正確順序為 ②③④①。

items.prompt: Rajan：Saki, what’s the list for?Saki：It’s not just a list. It’s a recipe for beef curry.Rajan：Wait. What’s this? Chocolate?Saki：No, it’s a block of curry. That makes it possible to easily prepare a perfect pot of curry every time.Rajan：Interesting! I’ve never used that in India. Saki：＿1.＿ A lot of people even call curry “a national food of Japan” and eat curry often.Rajan：I see. I think Japan has had its own styles of curry.Saki：Right. Have you ever tried Japanese curry?Rajan：No. Saki：＿2.＿Rajan：Sure, I don’t mind giving it a try.Saki：How’s the curry?Rajan：It’s delicious, but it’s very different from Indian curry.Saki：How are they different?Rajan：＿3.＿, Japanese curry is much thicker, and the taste is on the sweeter side. Besides, in the area of India where I come from, “curry” means any meat or vegetables with sauce. There are a lot of types of curry, for example, yogurt-based curry, tomato-based curry, and the list goes on and on. Saki：＿4.＿ So, everything is curry, but also nothing is curry. Rajan：You can say that again. Saki：Nobody taught me that before. Now I’m ＿5.＿ learning more about your curry! recipe 食譜 curry 咖哩 pot 鍋子 sauce 醬汁 yogurt-based 以優格為底的 tomato-based 以番茄為底的（ ）1. (A) Making curry has never been simple or easy. (B) I hope this has taught you more about Japan’s history. (C) Curry has been popular all over Japan for many years. (D) Curry has been the worst menu item at restaurants for many years.（ ）2. (A) Do you have any interest in trying it? (B) Do you think this curry recipe is from India? (C) Do you love my country because we have curry? (D) Do you know Japanese curry and Indian curry are different?（ ）3. (A) Finally (B) In a word (C) First of all (D) For this reason（ ）4. (A) Excellent! (B) What a surprise! (C) It’s a boring story. (D) That sounds scary.（ ）5. (A) tired of (B) scared of (C) bored with (D) interested in
choices: Making curry has never been simple or easy.
I hope this has taught you more about Japan’s history.
Curry has been popular all over Japan for many years.
Curry has been the worst menu item at restaurants for many years.（ ）2.
Do you have any interest in trying it?
Do you think this curry recipe is from India?
Do you love my country because we have curry?
Do you know Japanese curry and Indian curry are different?（ ）3.
items.explanation: 1. 由後句許多人稱咖哩是日本的國民美食，並且很常吃，可知是敘述「長年以來，咖哩一直在日本全國都受到歡迎」。2. 由後句 Rajan 回答「我不介意給它一次機會」，可知 Saki 是問他「你有興趣嘗試看看嗎？」。3. 由後句的轉折語 Besides 可知，Rajan 在舉例說明兩者的差異。first of all 表示「首先」，用在第一個例子的前面。4. 由於 Rajan 向 Saki 說明過去沒人告訴過她的知識，Saki 應會對此感到驚訝，故選 What a surprise! 最符合前後語意。5. 由 Saki 想要學習更多的印度咖哩知識，可知她對此資訊內容「感到有興趣」。

items.prompt: The yoga world has lost one of its greatest teachers. On October 13th, Indra Jois died quietly in her sleep at the age of 87. When Ms. Jois was just eight years old, she saw a group of boys making strange shapes on a beach in India. Though she didn’t know ＿1.＿, she thought they looked beautiful and funny at the same time. She wanted to join them, but she had no idea ＿2.＿. So, she went back there every day and practiced making strange shapes like them with her body. As time went on, the boys even welcomed her and made her a part of their yoga family. Before long, she was able to do more and better than the boys. Ms. Jois knew that she needed to find a better and stronger teacher, ＿3.＿. At first, the teacher didn’t want to teach her because she was a woman, but when she called him a snob, ＿4.＿. Ms. Jois learned from him for almost twenty years before she started teaching yoga herself. In her fifty years of teaching, Ms. Jois taught everyone from children to world leaders. She touched a lot of people, and she sure will be missed by the world. yoga 瑜珈 snob 自負傲慢的人 leader 領袖（ ）1. (A) what doing were they (B) what were they doing (C) what doing they were (D) what they were doing（ ）2. (A) who can she ask (B) who can ask (C) who to ask (D) who she asked（ ）3. (A) but she didn’t feel like that (B) so that was what she did (C) so she told him how to learn (D) although that was what hurt her（ ）4. (A) he changed his mind (B) he got really mad and hit her (C) he decided to give her just a few tips (D) he said she was lying to him

so that was what she did
so she told him how to learn
although that was what hurt her（ ）4.
he got really mad and hit her

items.prompt: A Symbol of Love: A Mail Carrier’s Taj Mahal Today, we are bringing you a story about a person in India. He was so much in love with his wife, and he built a Taj Mahal for her after she died. The person is not a rich man or a king of some big land. This one is just a common man. Faizul Hasan Qadri is an 81-year-old retired post office clerk. Qadri and Tajammuli got married in 1953. However, Qadri lost Tajammuli to throat cancer in 2011. After that, he began building his little Taj Mahal in memory of his dear wife. Qadri wants to finish the building before he dies, and then he wants to be by her side. “I have to do it on my own,” he said. For years, Qadri has been building his Taj Mahal outside his house. In fact, he has spent all of his money and sold some of his land to get enough money to finish the job. Qadri has become a famous person because of his Taj Mahal and his love to Tajammuli. Visitors from all over have come here to see this beautiful symbol of love. Let’s pray his dreams come true! article 文章 symbol 象徵 retired 退休的 marry 結婚 cancer 癌症 memory 紀念 pray 祈禱（ ）1. What is the reading mainly about? (A) A king’s family history. (B) A wonderful trip to India. (C) A husband’s love for his wife. (D) The ways to go for one’s dream.（ ）2. What does “it” refer to in the reading? refer to 意指 (A) Getting people to visit India. (B) Asking for help with money. (C) Building the little Taj Mahal. (D) Finding a place to build his home.（ ）3. What can we learn from the reading? (A) Qadri’s Taj Mahal has been there since 1953. (B) Qadri didn’t start to build his Taj Mahal until his wife died. (C) Qadri has worked with his wife on their Taj Mahal for years. (D) Although Qadri is 81 years old, he works as a mail carrier to make money.
choices: A husband’s love for his wife.
The ways to go for one’s dream.（ ）2. What does “it” refer to in the reading? refer to 意指
Finding a place to build his home.（ ）3. What can we learn from the reading?
Qadri’s Taj Mahal has been there since 1953.
Qadri didn’t start to build his Taj Mahal until his wife died.
Qadri has worked with his wife on their Taj Mahal for years.
Although Qadri is 81 years old, he works as a mail carrier to make money.
items.explanation: 1. 由標題 a symbol of love 與第一段末 He built a Taj Mahal for her after she died. 可知，文章主要在描述一位丈夫對妻子的愛，因此在她去世後，決定建造一座仿泰姬瑪哈陵來紀念她。2. 由前句 Qadri wants to finish the building before he dies…，以及後句說他這些年花了許多心力與金錢在這座仿泰姬瑪哈陵上可知 it 是指「建造仿泰姬瑪哈陵」。3. 由第一段可知，仿泰姬瑪哈陵是為了紀念妻子，因此 Qadri 是在妻子過世後才開始建造該建築。

items.prompt: Jeff：Hi, you must be the new guy. I’m going to show you the ropes today.Rick：Thanks! This is my first week working at BIG Supermarket.Jeff：First, let’s start from the back. We put important groceries like eggs and milk there so that people will have to go through the whole store to get them. Perhaps they will pick up something on the way that they don’t plan to buy.Rick：I never knew the trick!Jeff：Another reason why the fridges are at the back of the store is it takes less time for the delivery trucks to stock them. We want to make sure they stay fresh the whole time.Rick：I see your point.Jeff：Next, you can see we put up nutritional information signs for some items. These not only make us a responsible store but also stand out and help customers choose which to buy. Sometimes, they can be helpful when it’s something we want to sell more.Rick：Sounds very smart. Let me take some notes.Jeff：At the end of the aisles, we put items that are on sale. These are usually products that people might not need or have on their grocery lists.Rick：So when they see the good deals, they can’t help but put them in the cart! This is amazing!Jeff：You’ve got it! Lastly, have you noticed where we put the small packages of things?Rick：I know they are usually placed where people line up to pay, but is there also a reason behind it?Jeff：Of course! After shopping in the store for some time, people get tired of making all the choices. So this is when they usually just pick up the chocolate, for example, without thinking it twice.Rick：Wow, there’s so much about how customers think and do behind a simple act. Thanks for sharing with me! grocery 雜貨 whole 整個的 stock 備貨 nutritional 營養的 responsible 有責任感的 notes 筆記 aisle 走道 cart 購物推車（ ）1. What does Jeff mean when he says “show you the ropes”? (A) To teach Rick how to do a job. (B) To prepare some tools for Rick. (C) To expect Rick to show up on time. (D) To show Rick some products at the store.（ ）2. (A) Nutritional information is helpful for people who don’t make shopping lists. (B) There are many tricks that stores play to make customers spend more. (A) 對話僅提到附上營養標示招牌的產品較顯眼且能夠幫助消費者選擇，並非給沒有購物清單的人們；(C) 由倒數第二個 Rick 可知，消費者傾向在排隊結帳時挑選小包裝的產品；(D) 由第二個 Jeff 可知，牛奶及蛋類通常置放於商店裡的後方以保新鮮。

items.prompt: Have you ever seen a pumpkin that looks like a nose or an apple that looks like a funny face? They may not look great, but they taste just as good as the pretty ones. These strange-looking fruit and vegetables are called “seconds.” About 20-40% of what farmers grow is not so beautiful. Sadly, these “seconds” seldom arrive at your table, but often go straight into the trash can. Why? It’s because supermarkets don’t want to buy them from farmers—they believe their shoppers only love beautiful things. Because of these “seconds,” some farmers lose a lot of money. Wonky Markt wishes to change this. We’re helping sell these “seconds.” Farmers can save them from the trash can, and you can get them at a lower price.Send us photos of your delicious dishes that are made with our “seconds” to oneandonly@wonkymarkt.com, and you may win our cookbook. service charge 手續費【106教育會考】（ ）1. What does Wonky Markt care about? (A) Supermarkets often sell “seconds” at a lower price. (B) Farmers don’t know how to grow fewer “seconds.” (C) “Seconds” are thrown away because of how they look. (D) People don’t know much about picking fresh “seconds.”（ ）2. What do we know about buying the “seconds” from Wonky Markt? (A) You can save 20-40% if you shop for a second time. (B) If you buy three boxes, you will need to pay NT$900. (C) You can choose not only their size but also their shape. (D) To win the cookbook, you need to buy at least six boxes.
choices: Supermarkets often sell “seconds” at a lower price.
Farmers don’t know how to grow fewer “seconds.”
“Seconds” are thrown away because of how they look.
People don’t know much about picking fresh “seconds.”（ ）2. What do we know about buying the “seconds” from Wonky Markt?
You can save 20-40% if you shop for a second time.
If you buy three boxes, you will need to pay NT$900.
You can choose not only their size but also their shape.
To win the cookbook, you need to buy at least six boxes.
items.explanation: 1. 由廣告第一段可知 seconds 是指好吃卻因為外型不好看而被農夫丟棄的蔬果，第二段則是說明 Wonky Markt 想以低價販售這些 seconds，幫農夫減少損失，也幫消費者省錢。由此推斷 Wonky Markt 在乎這些因為外型不好而被浪費丟棄的 seconds（瑕疵品），故選 (C)。2. 由廣告第二段中間的消費須知可知，每箱蔬果臺幣 250 元，未滿 1,000 元，每箱需支付手續費 50 元，因此，若買三箱，則需要 250×3＋50×3＝900元，故選 (B)。另，20-40% 是說明農夫種出不美蔬果的比率，而不是省下的錢，故不選 (A)；廣告中說能挑選的是蔬果種類，而不是它們的外觀形狀，故不選 (C)；要贏得食譜，得用該店的產品做出佳餚上傳照片到網站，而不是要買到六箱，故不選 (D)。

items.prompt: Playing sports at least three times a week good for your health.【105教育會考】(A) is (B) are (C) has (D) have
items.explanation: 動名詞（Playing...）當主詞表單數，而空格後為形容詞片語 good for（對……好），故空格應填入表單數的 be 動詞，故選 (A)。
